core.text: California should loosen existing firearm restrictions.
California should restrict Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) enforcement operations within the state.
California should protect legal access to abortion.
The state should avoid raising taxes to balance its budget.
California's tax system should place a larger share of the tax burden on higher earners.
California should make tuition free at public colleges and universities for students.
Social goals are best reached through capitalism rather than socialism.
California should restrict automated license plate readers and similar technologies.
The state should increase the building of affordable housing.
California should create a single-payer health care system, in which one public program covers all residents.
California should reduce government regulations that slow down housing construction.
The state should quickly build emergency housing where people can spend nights indoors with access to care.
The state should create universal pre-K for all families.
California should support a path to citizenship for undocumented immigrants.

statements.text: California should create a single-payer health care system, in which one public program covers all residents.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra: He states that health care is a human right, will strengthen Medi-Cal, and will build toward Medicare for All.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_katie_porter: Porter supports single-payer health care, known in California as CalCare, and would deliver it as governor.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_raji_rab: Supports Medicare for All and full, free health care for every American.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer: Steyer says he will deliver single-payer health care, paid for by closing corporate tax giveaways.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond: Would establish a single-payer health care system.

statements.raceInsight: Health care costs and coverage affect nearly every Californian's budget and access to doctors. The governor's stance on how the state organizes coverage shapes what happens to state health programs and state taxes.
statements.policyBackground: A single-payer system uses one public insurance program to pay for health care instead of many private insurers. Medicare for All is a national version of this model, and CalCare is a California proposal of the same type. Supporters argue it simplifies billing and covers everyone, while critics raise concerns about cost and taxes.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: I know that health care is a human right. As California’s Health Care Governor I will deliver affordable care without debt or delays, strengthen Medi-Cal, close racial and economic gaps, and build toward Medicare for All.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: Single payer – known in California as CalCare – will deliver the highest quality AND most cost-effective care to the MOST people. Every policymaker should want that.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I believe that healthcare rights are human rights, and every American deserves full and free healthcare with Medicare for All.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: As Governor, I will repair this broken bargain, by delivering single-payer healthcare, and with strong revenue policies that close corporate giveaways to raise billions in new funding.

ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond.quote: Establish a single-payer health care system

statements.text: California should protect legal access to abortion.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra: As governor, he will ensure California continues to lead in protecting access to abortion.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_katie_porter: Porter says California must remain a state that protects and defends abortion rights, and she will do so as governor.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_raji_rab: Supports women's right to reproductive health care access and privacy, including legal protection for out-of-state abortion patients and shielding their medical records.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond: Supports abortion care that is legal and accessible.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz: He would enforce a right to abortion and bodily autonomy.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri: He would close Planned Parenthood's ability to operate in California.

statements.raceInsight: Abortion rules have changed sharply since 2022 when federal protections ended, and California has become a destination for patients from other states. State law now determines how care is available, funded, and protected.
statements.policyBackground: Abortion policy in the United States has shifted between federal and state control. California law sets the rules for providing and protecting abortion within the state. Debates include whether the state should expand legal protections and how to protect patients who travel from other states.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: As Governor, I will ensure that California continues to lead when it comes to protecting access to abortion, to the ballot, and to live and love without restraint.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: California must remain a state that protects and defends abortion rights and when I’m Governor we will.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I support women's right for reproductive health care access and privacy, legally protecting women who travel from other states to access abortion services here in California, including shielding their medical records.

ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond.quote: That's why he's fighting for a tax on billionaires, healthcare for all, abolishing ICE, 2 million new units of housing, finally fully funding our public schools, abortion care that is legal and accessible, getting weapons of war off of our streets, and protecting democracy.

ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri.quote: Close down and remove Planned (Abortions) Parenthood’s ability to operate in the State of California.

ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz.quote: We'll enforce bodily autonomy rights, to abortion, assisted suicides and guns.

statements.text: State government should negotiate prices for prescription drugs that it buys for public programs.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra: He will negotiate maximum reimbursement rates for drugs bought through state programs and prioritize lower-cost biosimilars and therapeutic alternatives where clinically appropriate.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_satish_rao: Supports using the state, through Medi-Cal, to negotiate better prices against the health industry.

statements.raceInsight: Prescription drug spending is a large part of state health budgets, and high drug prices affect patients and taxpayers alike. How the state buys medicines determines how much it pays for coverage.
statements.policyBackground: Drug price negotiation means a government buyer seeks lower prices from drug makers in exchange for coverage or volume. Medi-Cal is California's public health coverage program for low-income residents, and it is one of the state's largest drug purchasers. Critics question whether negotiation affects drug supply or innovation.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: I will negotiate maximum reimbursement rates for drugs purchased through state employee health plans, Medi-Cal, and all state-administered programs, and direct agencies to prioritize lower-cost biosimilars and therapeutic alternatives wherever clinically appropriate.

ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.quote: Individuals have no chance against the powerful health industry, whereas the state, through Medi-Cal, can negotiate a better deal.

statements.text: California should require children to be vaccinated before attending public school.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri: He would publicly nullify SB 276 and SB 277, which he says infringe on religious exemptions.

statements.raceInsight: School vaccination rules affect whether children can attend classes and how well communities are protected from diseases such as measles. California has changed these rules in recent years, so the question remains active.
statements.policyBackground: California's school vaccine law sets which vaccines students must have before enrollment and which exemptions are allowed. SB 277, passed in 2015, limited certain exemptions. Supporters argue requirements protect public health, while opponents argue they should not override personal or religious beliefs.

ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri.quote: Publicly nullify SB 276 and SB 277 that illegally infringe upon the 1st Amendment and religious exemption which discriminate against parents and their children who choose not to vaccinate.

statements.text: The state should act to prevent reductions in Medi-Cal coverage, California's health program for low-income residents.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra: On day one, he will issue an executive order to maintain coverage continuity for Californians affected by federal cuts or Medi-Cal rollbacks.

statements.raceInsight: Medi-Cal covers millions of Californians, and federal and state budget decisions can change who qualifies and what services are included. Changes to the program affect both patients and hospitals and clinics that serve them.
statements.policyBackground: Medi-Cal is California's version of Medicaid, the joint federal-state health program for low-income people. When federal funding or state budgets shrink, eligibility and benefits can be reduced. Debates focus on whether the state should use its own funds to protect coverage when cuts occur.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: On Day One, I will issue an executive order directing state agencies to maintain coverage continuity for every Californian affected by federal cuts or Medi-Cal rollbacks.

statements.text: Planned Parenthood should be allowed to operate in California.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri: He would close Planned Parenthood's ability to operate in California.

statements.raceInsight: Planned Parenthood runs many clinics across California that provide reproductive health services to a large number of patients. Whether these clinics can operate affects access to care in many communities.
statements.policyBackground: Planned Parenthood is a nonprofit health provider that offers services including contraception, cancer screening, testing for sexually transmitted infections, and abortion in some locations. Debates concern whether the state should support or limit its operation and funding.

ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri.quote: Close down and remove Planned (Abortions) Parenthood’s ability to operate in the State of California.

statements.text: The state should limit state-funded health services for immigrants to the services federal rules allow, rather than covering those federal rules exclude.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra: He will direct state agencies to protect access to essential health services from federal restrictions, including healthcare for immigrant communities.

statements.raceInsight: Federal rules set limits on which immigrants can get publicly funded health coverage, and California's choices here affect many families, clinics, and hospitals across the state. Voters often weigh public health access against state costs.
statements.policyBackground: Federal rules set eligibility limits for some health programs, and certain immigrants may be excluded from federal coverage. State-funded services are health programs paid for with state money instead of federal funds.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: I will also direct state agencies to protect access to essential, medically appropriate health services from federal restrictions, including reproductive care and healthcare for immigrant communities, and ensure uninterrupted, equitable access to contraception, abortion, and maternal health support.

statements.draft: The state should use its own agencies to keep essential health services available to immigrants, even when federal rules restrict them.

statements.text: California should create a dedicated task force to investigate and prosecute fraud in Medi-Cal, with power to hold funds and file charges.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra: He will create a dedicated healthcare fraud task force with authority to hold funds, investigate, file charges, and pursue cases to verdict.

statements.raceInsight: Medi-Cal is one of the largest state-funded programs in California, so questions about how well public health dollars are protected matter to taxpayers. Voters often weigh how aggressively the state should police program spending.
statements.policyBackground: Medi-Cal is California's state-run health program for low-income residents, funded by state and federal money. A fraud task force is a specialized team that looks into false claims and misuse of program funds. Holding funds means temporarily freezing payments that are under investigation.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: I will create a dedicated healthcare fraud task force with the authority to hold funds, investigate bad actors, file charges, and see cases through to verdict.

statements.text: Large employers should not be required to pay a fee to the state when they do not offer health coverage to low-wage workers.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra: He will pursue a fee on large employers who do not offer health coverage to low-wage workers who qualify for Medi-Cal.

statements.raceInsight: Many low-wage Californians rely on Medi-Cal because their jobs do not include health insurance, which raises state costs. Voters often disagree on whether employers or taxpayers should cover that gap.
statements.policyBackground: An employer fee is a payment that a business must make to the government under a specific rule, such as failing to offer required coverage. Low-wage workers are employees earning pay at the lower end of the wage scale.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: I will pursue a fee on large employers who do not offer health coverage to their low-wage workers who qualify for Medi-Cal, so that corporations who shift their healthcare costs onto taxpayers pay their fair share.

statements.draft: Large employers that do not offer health coverage to low-wage workers should pay a fee to the state.

statements.text: Telehealth coverage for state-regulated health plans should be limited to what each plan chooses to offer, rather than mandated by state law.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra: He will require state-regulated payors to reimburse telehealth visits to the fullest extent permitted by law and expand specialty telehealth access.

statements.raceInsight: Many Californians live far from specialists or have trouble taking time off work, so remote visits can change how and where they get care. Voters often weigh convenience against concerns about quality and cost.
statements.policyBackground: Telehealth refers to medical visits conducted remotely by video or phone. State-regulated health plans are insurance plans overseen by state government, as opposed to plans regulated only at the federal level.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: As Governor, I will issue an executive order requiring all state-regulated payors to reimburse telehealth visits to the fullest extent permitted under law, prioritizing telehealth delivered by California-licensed health care professionals through local and regional providers to provide urgent care for conditions that do not require an in-person visit, and leverage California’s volunteer physician registry to open specialty telehealth access to communities that have never had it.

statements.draft: State-regulated health plans should be required to pay for telehealth visits to the fullest extent allowed by law.

statements.text: California should double state funding for reproductive health care and birth control access.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_raji_rab: Plans to double the existing $200 million for reproductive health care and birth control access.

statements.raceInsight: Access to reproductive health care and contraception is a major concern for many Californians and affects state health budgets. Voters often disagree about how much public money should go to these services.
statements.policyBackground: Reproductive health care includes services such as prenatal care, contraception, and family planning. California already funds these services with a set budget amount. Doubling the funding would raise that amount to a larger total in the state budget.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I will double the existing $200 million to expand access to reproductive health care and birth control.

statements.text: The state should offer a voluntary public health insurance option that competes with private health plans.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_serge_fiankan: Serge Fiankan proposes voluntary, region-specific public option pilots that compete with private plans.

statements.raceInsight: Health insurance premiums are a major cost for Californians, and voters often disagree about whether government plans would improve choice or affect private insurers. This question shapes how coverage is offered across the state.
statements.policyBackground: A public option is a government-run health plan that people can choose instead of a private insurer. Supporters describe it as a lower-cost choice, while critics raise questions about its effect on private plans. Pilot programs test an approach in limited areas before wider use.

ca_gov_primary_serge_fiankan.quote: The public option is voluntary and structured as region-specific pilots that compete with private plans.

statements.text: The state should ban surprise medical bills, meaning bills patients get for care they did not choose from an out-of-network provider.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_serge_fiankan: Serge Fiankan proposes a full surprise billing ban and requires hospitals to publish upfront prices.

statements.raceInsight: Patients often receive large bills from providers they did not select, such as an out-of-network doctor at an in-network hospital. Voters commonly weigh protections for patients against the rights of providers to set their own rates.
statements.policyBackground: A surprise bill occurs when a patient is charged the full out-of-network price for care they did not choose. Bans limit or stop these charges and often set how disputes between insurers and providers are resolved. The policy is usually discussed alongside other rules on medical billing.

ca_gov_primary_serge_fiankan.quote: The plan targets cost drivers people can see: upfront pricing, a full surprise billing ban, prevention-first coverage, and competition through capped public option pilots.

statements.text: Hospitals should be required to publish their prices for care before patients receive it.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_serge_fiankan: Serge Fiankan proposes a full surprise billing ban and requires hospitals to publish upfront prices.

statements.raceInsight: Hospital prices vary widely and are often hard for patients to find before a procedure. Voters care about whether they can compare costs and plan for expenses.
statements.policyBackground: Price transparency rules require hospitals to share their charges, often in advance, so patients and insurers can compare them. Supporters say this helps people shop for care, while others question how useful the information is in practice. Upfront prices are quoted before a service is delivered.

ca_gov_primary_serge_fiankan.quote: The plan targets cost drivers people can see: upfront pricing, a full surprise billing ban, prevention-first coverage, and competition through capped public option pilots.

statements.text: Californians should be allowed to buy health insurance sold by companies based in other states.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri: He would let Californians buy and accept health insurance across state lines to increase competition and choice.

statements.raceInsight: Health insurance costs and the number of plan choices affect many households and small businesses. Voters often disagree about whether allowing out-of-state plans would lower prices or weaken state consumer protections.
statements.policyBackground: Currently, health insurers generally must be licensed in each state where they sell plans, and state rules set coverage requirements. Allowing sales across state lines would let residents buy plans approved in another state. Supporters cite more competition, while critics raise concerns about oversight.

ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri.quote: Create a state healthcare policy that will allow Californians to buy and accept health insurances across our state line to create better competition and choice.

statements.text: The federal agency Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) should be abolished.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_katie_porter: Porter says she will work with federal partners to abolish ICE.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer: Steyer called for abolishing ICE and proposed that California criminally prosecute ICE agents and leadership.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_ramsey_robinson: Opposes deportations and supports abolishing ICE.

statements.raceInsight: ICE carries out immigration arrests and deportations in California, so whether the agency should exist in its current form affects many families and communities across the state. Voters often weigh this question alongside concerns about public safety and border control.
statements.policyBackground: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is a federal agency responsible for finding, arresting, and removing people who are in the United States without legal permission. Abolishing it would require action by the federal government, and proposals to do so usually involve shifting its duties to other agencies or new structures.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: That’s why I will work with our federal partners to Abolish ICE.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: In an April 2026 essay on his Substack, paired with a post on X (formerly Twitter), Steyer called for the abolition of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and proposed that California criminally prosecute ICE agents and leadership, end racial profiling through state legislation, expand California's immigration legal-defence infrastructure, and conduct public education on immigrants' rights.

ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond.quote: That's why he's fighting for a tax on billionaires, healthcare for all, abolishing ICE, 2 million new units of housing, finally fully funding our public schools, abortion care that is legal and accessible, getting weapons of war off of our streets, and protecting democracy.

ca_gov_primary_ramsey_robinson.quote: Stop deportations, abolish ICE!

statements.topic: State and local police cooperation with ICE
statements.text: California should limit how state and local police cooperate with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond: Would protect California's sanctuary state laws.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_chad_bianco: Attended a press conference promoting a bill to weaken SB 54's limits on law enforcement cooperation with ICE.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri: Would stop any city or town from providing sanctuary to illegal aliens and prosecute officials who do.

statements.raceInsight: Whether local police help federal immigration agents affects how residents of cities and counties interact with law enforcement. Many Californians care about both immigration enforcement and trust between local police and immigrant communities.
statements.policyBackground: California has laws that restrict how local police and jails share information with and assist federal immigration agents, and these rules are often called sanctuary policies. Supporters of limits argue they keep local officers focused on local crime, while opponents argue they can prevent cooperation that helps remove people with criminal records.

ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond.quote: Protect California’s sanctuary state laws

ca_gov_primary_chad_bianco.quote: On February 21, Bianco attended a press conference in San Diego with Republican leaders to promote State Senate Republican Minority Leader Brian Jones ' proposed bill SB554 to weaken the California Senate Bill 54 of 2017 that limits law enforcement's ability to cooperate with ICE.

ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri.quote: As governor, I will no longer allow any city or town, non-incorporated or incorporated the ability to provide “sanctuary” to any illegal alien, permanently!

statements.text: California should restrict Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) enforcement operations within the state.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_derek_grasty: Would keep ICE off California's streets.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_erin_zez_zezulak: States that ICE will not be permitted in California using its present tactics.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_livingforgod_andcountry_d: Has a plan to stop illegal ICE operations.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer: Steyer called for abolishing ICE and proposed that California criminally prosecute ICE agents and leadership.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_chad_bianco: He attended a press conference promoting a bill to weaken SB 54's limits on law enforcement cooperation with ICE.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_ramsey_robinson: Opposes deportations and supports abolishing ICE.

statements.raceInsight: ICE street operations and raids affect workplaces, neighborhoods, and schools across California. Voters differ on how much the state should limit federal enforcement activity within its borders.
statements.policyBackground: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is the federal agency that conducts immigration arrests and removals inside the United States. State governments have limited power to direct federal agents, so any restriction would depend on state laws, state agency rules, or legal challenges in court.

ca_gov_primary_derek_grasty.quote: Together, we will keep kidnappers (ICE) off our streets, make housing affordable for working families, first responders, teachers, firefighters, and nurses.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: In an April 2026 essay on his Substack, paired with a post on X (formerly Twitter), Steyer called for the abolition of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and proposed that California criminally prosecute ICE agents and leadership, end racial profiling through state legislation, expand California's immigration legal-defence infrastructure, and conduct public education on immigrants' rights.

ca_gov_primary_erin_zez_zezulak.quote: ICE will not be permitted in California using its present tactics.

ca_gov_primary_chad_bianco.quote: On February 21, Bianco attended a press conference in San Diego with Republican leaders to promote State Senate Republican Minority Leader Brian Jones ' proposed bill SB554 to weaken the California Senate Bill 54 of 2017 that limits law enforcement's ability to cooperate with ICE.

ca_gov_primary_ramsey_robinson.quote: Stop deportations, abolish ICE!

ca_gov_primary_livingforgod_andcountry_d.quote: I have a plan to STOP illegal ICE operations; and a chaplain's heart to remember who the system serves.

statements.topic: Path to citizenship for undocumented immigrants
statements.text: California should support a path to citizenship for undocumented immigrants.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_raji_rab: Supports immigration amnesty for undocumented people who pay a fee, as a signature issue.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond: Would work with Congress to establish a pathway to citizenship.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_margaret_trowe: Calls for a union-backed fight for amnesty for undocumented workers to build working-class unity.

statements.raceInsight: California has a large undocumented population, and questions about legal status affect workers, families, and employers throughout the state. Voters often weigh this issue against concerns about border security and the rule of law.
statements.policyBackground: A path to citizenship would give people living in the country without legal status a way to become lawful permanent residents and later citizens. Such changes are generally made through federal immigration law, and past proposals have included conditions such as fees, background checks, or waiting periods.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I support immigration Amnesty as my signature issue as it has become a humanitarian issue, an integrity issue and an issue of human dignity. It's time to face reality and embrace those already here, living with us and helping us for years in meeting our low budget and affordability crisis in so many areas of our daily lives.

ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond.quote: Work with Congress to establish a pathway to citizenship

ca_gov_primary_margaret_trowe.quote: Calls for union-backed fight for amnesty for undocumented workers to build working-class unity.

statements.topic: Ban on ICE agents wearing masks
statements.text: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents should be banned from wearing masks while on duty.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_eric_swalwell: Said ICE would be more credible without masks and advocated tying ICE's funding to a ban on agents wearing masks on duty.

statements.raceInsight: Voters differ on whether federal agents should be identifiable during enforcement actions. The question touches on accountability, public trust, and officer safety.
statements.policyBackground: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents sometimes wear face coverings during arrests and operations. A mask ban would require agents to show their faces while on duty, and such a rule would raise questions about federal authority over its own officers.

ca_gov_primary_eric_swalwell.quote: Swalwell said that ICE would be more credible if they did not wear masks, and advocated for legislation that would tie ICE's funding to a ban on agents wearing masks in the course of their duties.

statements.topic: Tax on companies that run ICE detention centers
statements.text: Companies operating Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention centers should not be taxed by the state for that work.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond: Would levy a tax on companies that operate ICE detention centers.

statements.raceInsight: Detention centers house people held during immigration proceedings, and the companies that run them receive public funds. Voters weigh how much the state should respond to private operators of federal detention facilities.
statements.policyBackground: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is a federal agency that enforces immigration law, including by holding people in detention. Detention centers are facilities where people are held while their immigration cases proceed. A state tax is a charge collected by California's government on business activity.

ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond.quote: Levy a tax on companies that operate ICE detention centers

statements.draft: Companies that operate Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention centers should pay a tax to the state.

statements.text: California should suspend the processing of refugee and asylum seekers entering the state.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri: Would place a moratorium on the state's borders, suspending review or processing of refugee and asylum seekers into California.

statements.raceInsight: Refugee and asylum policy shapes who can enter and remain in the country, and debates over it often involve humanitarian obligations and border management. Voters differ on the role a state government should play in these decisions.
statements.policyBackground: Refugees and asylum seekers are people who seek protection from persecution in another country, and their claims are reviewed under federal law. Federal authority generally controls admission and asylum decisions, so a state-level pause would raise legal questions about the scope of state power.

ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri.quote: Place a moratorium on our state’s southern, northern, and coastal borders, suspending any further review or processing of refugee and asylum seekers into California.

statements.text: All Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention centers in California should be closed.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz: Would close all ICE detention centers.

statements.raceInsight: Detention centers in California hold people awaiting immigration decisions or removal, so decisions about them affect detainees, their families, and nearby communities. Voters differ on whether these facilities are necessary for immigration enforcement.
statements.policyBackground: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) operates detention centers where people are held during immigration proceedings. Closing them would require either federal agreement or state action on facilities and contracts, and detention is generally a federal function.

ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz.quote: We'll CLOSE ALL ICE DETENTION CENTERS, PROSECUTE CRIMES AGAINST HUMANITY, IF NECESSARY IN THE HAGUE!

statements.text: California voters should support Proposition 36, the 2024 measure that increased penalties for certain theft and drug crimes.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan: Endorsed California Proposition 36 in 2024, which increased sentences for certain theft and drug related crimes.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_elaine_culotti: Supports Proposition 36 with stronger constraints and immediate funding.

statements.raceInsight: Criminal penalties for theft and drug offenses affect public safety, court workloads, and jail populations across the state, so voters want to know where candidates stand on the measures that set them.
statements.policyBackground: Proposition 36 was a statewide ballot measure approved by voters in 2024. It increased sentences for certain theft and drug-related crimes, changing how some repeat offenses are charged and punished.

ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.quote: In 2024, in contrast to other state Democratic leaders, he endorsed California Proposition 36, which increased sentences for certain theft and drug related crimes.

ca_gov_primary_chad_bianco.quote: Bianco has portrayed himself as a law and order candidate, and supported Proposition 36.

ca_gov_primary_elaine_culotti.quote: Support Proposition 36 with stronger constraints and immediate funding

statements.text: California should offer diversion to treatment programs for people charged with drug offenses instead of prosecution.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_satish_rao: Favors New York-style drug law overhaul and focused diversion-to-treatment programs to lower incarceration without sacrificing safety.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_serge_fiankan: Supports diversion only for non-violent, low-risk cases proven to reduce reoffending, with failure returning cases to prosecution.

statements.raceInsight: How the justice system handles drug cases shapes prison crowding, treatment access, and public safety in communities across California.
statements.policyBackground: Diversion lets a person charged with a crime complete a program, such as drug treatment, in place of a criminal case proceeding through the courts. Programs usually set eligibility rules and may return a case to prosecution if the person does not complete the program.

ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.quote: New York has proven that a state can drastically lower incarceration rates without sacrificing public safety, provided the government commits to focused, verifiable diversion programs rather than endlessly funding a massive prison bureaucracy.

ca_gov_primary_serge_fiankan.quote: Diversion is allowed for non-violent, low-risk cases only when it is proven to reduce reoffending.

statements.text: California should increase enforcement against drug trafficking.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan: Publicly supported stronger enforcement against drug trafficking in 2023 and 2024, while also promoting expanded treatment options.

statements.raceInsight: Fentanyl and other illegal drugs have driven overdose deaths in California, making enforcement against trafficking a central question for voters.
statements.policyBackground: Drug trafficking enforcement covers police investigations, arrests, and prosecutions of people who manufacture, sell, or move illegal drugs. Debate often centers on how enforcement should be balanced with treatment and prevention.

ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.quote: In 2023 and 2024, Mahan publicly supported stronger enforcement against drug trafficking while also promoting expanded treatment options.

statements.text: California should impose the death penalty for some crimes.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri: Supports reinstating and fast-tracking the death penalty for child pedophiles and similar predators.

statements.raceInsight: The death penalty is one of the most debated criminal justice questions in California, where executions have been paused for years and voters have weighed in repeatedly.
statements.policyBackground: The death penalty is a sentence of execution for a person convicted of certain serious crimes. Supporters and opponents disagree on its fairness, its deterrent effect, and the risk of executing an innocent person.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I do not support death penalty.

ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri.quote: Re-institution and a fast track to the death penalty for all child pedophiles and various predators alike.

statements.text: Police departments should hire more officers.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa: Says he hired nearly one thousand new police officers, increasing the LAPD force to over 10,000 for the first time in history.

statements.raceInsight: Staffing levels in police departments affect response times and workloads, and California cities differ on how many officers they can fund.
statements.policyBackground: Police staffing refers to the number of sworn officers a department employs. Cities and counties set staffing levels through budgets, and debate often focuses on whether more officers reduce crime and how hiring costs compare with other public services.

ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa.quote: Hired nearly one thousand new police officers, increasing the LAPD force to over 10,000 for the first time in history

statements.text: The state should invest more in crime prevention programs.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_akinyemi_agbede: Supports strengthening community policing and investing in crime prevention programs.

statements.raceInsight: Voters care about whether public money spent on preventing crime before it happens reduces violence and reduces the need for arrests and prisons.
statements.policyBackground: Crime prevention programs include youth outreach, violence interruption, and community-based services aimed at stopping crime before it occurs. Community policing is a model where officers work closely with residents on local safety problems.

ca_gov_primary_akinyemi_agbede.quote: Strengthening community policing efforts and investing in crime prevention programs to enhance security, build trust, and create safer neighborhoods.

statements.text: California should reform its juvenile justice system.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa: Says he led efforts to pass criminal justice and juvenile justice reforms, including more accountability at the LAPD.

statements.raceInsight: How the state handles young people who commit crimes affects their futures and the long-term safety of communities, and reform proposals have been debated for years.
statements.policyBackground: Juvenile justice systems handle cases involving minors, including arrests, court proceedings, detention, and rehabilitation. Reform proposals often focus on whether young offenders should be treated differently from adults and how programs support them.

ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa.quote: Led efforts to pass criminal justice reforms and juvenile justice reforms, including bringing reforms and more accountability to the LAPD

statements.text: The state should fund law enforcement task forces focused on domestic violence.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa: Says he secured funding to establish and expand a law enforcement task force to protect women and families from domestic violence.

statements.raceInsight: Domestic violence affects many California families, and voters often ask how state funds should support police and courts in responding to it.
statements.policyBackground: A task force is a team of officers and sometimes other agencies assigned to a specific problem. Domestic violence task forces typically investigate abuse in families and coordinate with victim services.

ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa.quote: Secured funding to establish and expand law enforcement task force to protect women and families from Domestic Violence

statements.text: Shoplifting under a set dollar threshold should be treated as an infraction rather than a crime.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_randeep_s_dhillon: Holds that shoplifting of any amount is a crime and that laws must be enforced fairly.

statements.raceInsight: Retail theft has been a concern for California businesses and shoppers, and debate continues over how theft laws should apply to low-dollar cases.
statements.policyBackground: An infraction is a minor offense that typically carries a fine rather than jail time, while a crime can carry more serious penalties. Shoplifting is taking merchandise from a store without paying. The rewrite describes the position of those who would reduce the classification of low-value theft.

ca_gov_primary_randeep_s_dhillon.quote: Shoplifting of any amount is a crime, and laws must be enforced fairly.

statements.draft: Shoplifting of any amount should be treated as a crime.

statements.text: Fusion centers should be used to investigate serious fraud, theft, and waste.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_naomi_bar_lev: Fusion centers would be used for serious investigations of fraud, theft, and waste, as a revenue source with a leaner budget.

statements.raceInsight: How government agencies investigate fraud and waste affects public money and the accountability of programs that California taxpayers fund.
statements.policyBackground: Fusion centers are facilities where government agencies share information and coordinate investigations. Debate covers their purpose, their budgets, and how they handle personal information.

ca_gov_primary_naomi_bar_lev.quote: As governor, fusion centers will be for serious investigations of fraud, theft, and waste, a healthy revenue source with a leaner budget.

statements.text: Police should return to neighborhood policing, with officers regularly assigned to specific communities.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_naomi_bar_lev: Police would return to neighborhoods, fight crime, take reports equally among citizens, and use a constitutionally compliant database.

statements.raceInsight: Whether officers are assigned to particular neighborhoods affects how residents experience policing and how quickly crimes are reported and investigated.
statements.policyBackground: Neighborhood policing assigns officers to specific areas so they build ongoing relationships with residents. Critics and supporters debate its effect on crime and on how fairly police treat different communities.

ca_gov_primary_naomi_bar_lev.quote: Police will return to neighborhoods, fighting crime, taking reports equally among citizens, using a constitutionally compliant database.

statements.text: New police officers should complete at least 12 more months of training before receiving arrest powers.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri: Would require at least 12 more months of training before an officer receives a badge, gun, investigative powers, and arrest power.

statements.raceInsight: How long officers train before working alone affects public trust and the quality of police response in California communities.
statements.policyBackground: Police academy and field training programs prepare recruits before they are authorized to make arrests and carry weapons. Debate centers on how much training is needed and what it costs local departments.

ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri.quote: We need required extended training for at least another 12 months before being granted a badge, a gun, perform investigations, and the power to arrest.

statements.text: County sheriff's departments should control their own budgets.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri: Would have county Sheriff budgets controlled by the Sheriff's department, with increases approved by county voters.

statements.raceInsight: Who controls the budget of a county sheriff affects jails, deputies, and how public money is spent on law enforcement in each county.
statements.policyBackground: A county sheriff is an elected official who leads law enforcement and runs the county jail in many California counties. County budgets are usually set by elected boards of supervisors, and debate centers on how much control sheriffs should have over their own funding.

ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri.quote: Under my administration, county Sheriff budgets will only be controlled by the Sheriff’s department and their increase by a vote of the people from their county.

statements.text: California should enact a new tax on the wealth of its wealthiest residents, such as billionaires.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell: Opposes a wealth tax, saying it is not the way to address California's challenges.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer: Wrote in January 2026 supporting a proposed one-off wealth tax in California.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond: Would establish a new tax on billionaires and centimillionaires.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz: Would enact a 5% wealth tax on assets over $10 million, plus a 5% income tax on income over $1 million.

statements.raceInsight: How the state taxes very large fortunes affects how much revenue is available for public services and how the tax burden is spread across residents. Voters often weigh this against concerns about capital leaving the state and how such taxes would be valued and enforced.
statements.policyBackground: A wealth tax is an annual or one-time charge on the total value of a person's assets, such as property, investments, and business holdings, rather than on income alone. Proposals usually set a minimum wealth level below which no tax applies. Supporters and opponents disagree about its revenue, administrative difficulty, and economic effects.

ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.quote: California is facing real challenges, and we need real solutions — but a wealth tax is not the way to go.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: In January 2026, he wrote an article supporting the proposed one-off wealth tax in California.

ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond.quote: Establish a new tax on billionaires and centimillionaires

ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz.quote: I WILL ENACT a 5% WEALTH TAX on the wealthiest Californians with over $10 Million, on their assets over $10 Million, approximately the richest 1.5% of CA's "households".

statements.text: California should eliminate state income tax for residents earning under $100,000.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_katie_porter: Would eliminate state income tax for Californians earning less than $100,000.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz: Would eliminate sales taxes and income taxes on income under $100,000.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_naomi_bar_lev: Sales, income, and property taxes would be eliminated.

statements.raceInsight: State income tax affects household budgets across income levels, and changes to it would reduce revenue that funds schools, health programs, and other services. Voters care about how any tax relief is targeted and how it would be paid for.
statements.policyBackground: State income tax is a tax on wages, investment earnings, and other income collected by California. Eliminating it for a given income group means residents below a set income level would owe no state income tax. The policy is debated because it reduces state revenue while lowering the tax burden on lower- and middle-income households.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: As Governor, I will work to eliminate state income tax for Californians making under $100,000. This will make a tangible difference in the lives of millions of people.

ca_gov_primary_naomi_bar_lev.quote: No sales, income, or property tax.

ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz.quote: NO MORE SALES TAXES OR INCOME TAXES UNDER $100K! WE CAN BARELY SURVIVE, MUCH LESS HAVE A FAMILY, AS IT IS! RENT FREEZE!

statements.text: California should raise taxes on large corporations.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_katie_porter: Would launch a progressive corporate tax that raises rates on the most profitable businesses.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer: Says he will close corporate tax loopholes and raise $20 billion in new revenue each year for education, healthcare, childcare, and home care.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_serge_fiankan: Serge Fiankan's tax plan keeps tiered corporate rates of 2.5% for small, 6% for mid, and 8% to 9% for large businesses.

statements.raceInsight: Corporate tax levels shape state revenue and how much large businesses contribute to public services. Voters weigh these changes against the effects on business investment, jobs, and prices.
statements.policyBackground: Corporate taxes are levied on the profits of businesses. A progressive corporate tax applies higher rates to larger profits, while closing loopholes removes tax breaks that reduce what companies owe. Both approaches are debated for their revenue potential and their effects on business decisions.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: As Governor, I will launch a Progressive Corporate Tax. This is more than a one time windfall: this is a thoughtful and permanent structural shift that will incentivize businesses to invest their revenues in paying workers and expanding operations.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: Tom is going to close these corporate loopholes, and raise $20 billion of new revenue each year to fund things like education, healthcare, childcare, and home care, all without charging working people a penny.

ca_gov_primary_serge_fiankan.quote: Tiered corporate rates are retained: small 2.5%, mid 6%, large 8% to 9%.

statements.text: California should lower taxes on businesses.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_elaine_culotti: Would bring jobs and investment back by reducing anti-growth tax burdens and regulatory drag.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_katie_porter: Porter would launch a progressive corporate tax that raises rates on the most profitable businesses.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer: Steyer says he will close corporate tax loopholes and raise $20 billion in new revenue each year for education, healthcare, childcare, and home care.

statements.raceInsight: Business tax levels influence where companies locate, how many jobs they create, and how much the state collects. Voters often compare the expected economic gains from lower business taxes with the revenue reductions needed to pay for public services.
statements.policyBackground: Business taxes include corporate income taxes and other levies that companies pay to the state. Lowering them is intended to make California more attractive for investment and employment. Critics argue that reduced business tax revenue may limit funding for public programs.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: As Governor, I will launch a Progressive Corporate Tax. This is more than a one time windfall: this is a thoughtful and permanent structural shift that will incentivize businesses to invest their revenues in paying workers and expanding operations.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: Tom is going to close these corporate loopholes, and raise $20 billion of new revenue each year to fund things like education, healthcare, childcare, and home care, all without charging working people a penny.

ca_gov_primary_elaine_culotti.quote: Bring jobs and investment back by reducing anti-growth tax burdens and regulatory drag.

statements.text: The state should lower income taxes on its highest earners.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri: Would nullify AB 1253 and cut the wealthy tax by half.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_naomi_bar_lev: Sales, income, and property taxes would be eliminated.

statements.raceInsight: Income taxes on the highest earners make up a large share of state revenue, so changes here affect the state budget. Voters weigh the fairness of how taxes are shared against the effect on revenue and on high earners' decisions to stay in California.
statements.policyBackground: Income tax rates in California rise with income, so high earners pay the highest rates. Proposals to lower these rates aim to reduce the tax burden on top earners, while proposals to add a tax on income above a threshold aim to raise revenue from the same group.

ca_gov_primary_naomi_bar_lev.quote: No sales, income, or property tax.

ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri.quote: Since AB 1253 is unconstitutional, I will nullify and cut the wealthy tax by half.

statements.text: California should eliminate the state sales tax.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_naomi_bar_lev: Would eliminate sales, income, and property taxes.

statements.raceInsight: Sales taxes apply to everyday purchases, so changes to them affect the cost of living for all residents. Voters weigh the relief this would bring against the revenue loss for public services.
statements.policyBackground: A sales tax is a percentage added to the price of most goods and some services at the point of sale. California collects a statewide sales tax on top of local add-ons. Eliminating it would lower prices for buyers but remove a major source of state revenue.

ca_gov_primary_naomi_bar_lev.quote: No sales, income, or property tax.

statements.text: California should eliminate property taxes.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_naomi_bar_lev: Would eliminate sales, income, and property taxes.

statements.raceInsight: Property taxes fund local schools, fire protection, and other services, and they affect homeowners and renters alike. Voters weigh the relief for property owners against the local funding that would be lost.
statements.policyBackground: Property taxes are charged on the assessed value of real estate, usually collected by local governments. California limits annual increases on assessed values for many properties. Eliminating these taxes would remove a major source of local government funding.

ca_gov_primary_naomi_bar_lev.quote: No sales, income, or property tax.

statements.text: Online retailers should be required to collect sales tax on purchases made by California customers.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_betty_t_yee: Led the successful effort to force Amazon to collect sales taxes on online purchases.

statements.raceInsight: Online shopping now accounts for a large share of retail sales, so how these sales are taxed affects state revenue and competition with local stores. Voters consider how to treat sellers fairly across online and in-person commerce.
statements.policyBackground: Sales tax collection rules determine whether sellers must add tax to purchases and send it to the state. Requiring online retailers to collect tax puts them on the same footing as stores with physical locations, and it affects how much revenue the state gathers from remote sales.

ca_gov_primary_betty_t_yee.quote: She led the successful effort to force Amazon to collect sales taxes on online purchases.

statements.text: Keeping household utility bills affordable should be a central goal of state energy policy.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra: Says bill affordability will be central to his energy policy, especially for low- and middle-income families.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_gretha_solorzano: Plans to lower utility costs for Californians.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_max_fomin: Says he will freeze utility rate hikes and cut red tape that raises housing costs.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_satish_rao: Reduce regulatory barriers to building power grids, water reservoirs, and housing so utilities and housing are more affordable.

statements.raceInsight: Electricity and gas bills affect nearly every household, and California's rates are among the higher ones in the country. Voters care about how state energy decisions change what they pay each month.
statements.policyBackground: Utility bills cover the cost of electricity and gas delivered to homes and businesses, including generation, transmission, and program charges. State regulators and lawmakers influence these costs through rate approvals and energy policy choices.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: Bill affordability will be at the center of my energy policy, especially for low- and middle-income families.

ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.quote: We must make it vastly easier and cheaper to build robust power grids, upgrade water reservoirs, and expand housing capacity so that basic utilities and housing are affordable for regular Californians.

ca_gov_primary_gretha_solorzano.quote: I will create jobs, lower utility costs, and deliver long-term growth for all Californians.

ca_gov_primary_max_fomin.quote: I will tackle the “California Tax” on everyday life. From freezing utility rate hikes to cutting the red tape that makes housing so expensive.

statements.text: California should adopt state rules that govern data center development.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra: Will require data centers in California to add value to the energy infrastructure, use clean energy, cover their own energy costs, and meet environmental disclosure requirements.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond: Would establish comprehensive regulations on data center development to ensure environmental and occupational safety.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer: Steyer says he will require data centers to ensure energy prices for families go down rather than up.

statements.raceInsight: Data centers use large amounts of electricity and water, and their growth is raising questions about grid capacity and utility costs in California. Voters want to know what rules will apply to new facilities.
statements.policyBackground: A data center is a building filled with computer servers that store and process internet and business data. Regulations can cover where such facilities are built, how they are powered, and what they must report about their environmental effects.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: I will pursue an economic-forward standard: data centers that operate in California add value to our current energy infrastructure, are powered with clean energy, cover the costs of their own energy needs, and meet environmental performance disclosure requirements.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: Tom will mandate that data centers ensure energy prices for families go down – not up.

ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond.quote: Establish comprehensive regulations on data center development to ensure environmental and occupational safety

statements.topic: Data centers and family energy prices
statements.text: Data centers should be required to keep energy prices for families from rising.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer: Says he will require data centers to ensure energy prices for families go down rather than up.

statements.raceInsight: Large new electricity users can shift the demand and cost picture for the whole grid. Voters want to know whether the costs of new data centers will fall on household bills.
statements.policyBackground: Energy prices for households depend on how much power is needed, how it is generated, and how the costs of grid upgrades are divided among customers. Rules for large customers are one way regulators can decide who pays for new infrastructure.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: Tom will mandate that data centers ensure energy prices for families go down – not up.

statements.text: The state should direct money now spent on foreign oil toward domestic production.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_gretha_solorzano: Plans strategic investments in advanced energy and water infrastructure, including redirecting the $32.7 billion spent on foreign oil toward domestic production.

statements.raceInsight: California imports a large share of its crude oil, so decisions about where fuel comes from affect prices and energy security. Voters have different views on how much the state should rely on local versus imported oil.
statements.policyBackground: Crude oil is the raw material refined into gasoline and diesel. Foreign oil is imported from other countries, while domestic production refers to oil produced within the United States.

ca_gov_primary_gretha_solorzano.quote: I will strengthen our economy through strategic investments in advanced energy and water infrastructure, including redirecting the $32.7 billion we currently spend on foreign oil toward domestic production to improve energy security and keep jobs here at home.

statements.text: California should support in-state crude oil production.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_randeep_s_dhillon: Supports responsible California crude oil production alongside renewable energy development.

statements.raceInsight: Oil drilling within California affects jobs, local fuel supply, and the state's climate goals. Voters weigh these trade-offs differently when deciding how much in-state oil production to allow.
statements.policyBackground: Crude oil is pumped from underground reservoirs and refined into fuels such as gasoline. State policy can regulate where and how drilling takes place and whether new production is permitted.

ca_gov_primary_randeep_s_dhillon.quote: I support responsible California crude oil production alongside renewable energy development to stabilize fuel costs, protect jobs, and reduce dependence on foreign energy.

statements.text: California should expand renewable energy as a major part of its energy supply.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_katie_porter: Aims to accelerate clean energy by investing in renewables and expanding the grid, with a goal of 100% clean energy output.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_raji_rab: Plans to set high standards for clean air and water, control carbon emissions, and expand renewable energy.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_randeep_s_dhillon: Supports responsible California crude oil production alongside renewable energy development.

statements.raceInsight: California has set ambitious targets for clean electricity, and the pace and cost of building renewable power affect utility bills and reliability. Voters differ on how quickly the state should shift its energy mix.
statements.policyBackground: Renewable energy comes from sources that naturally replenish, such as sunlight and wind. Expanding it typically involves building generation projects and upgrading the transmission grid that carries electricity to users.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: I will work to accelerate our transition to clean energy by investing in renewable resources like wind, solar, and geothermal, and expanding the grid to support these technologies.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: As your Governor I will set the highest standards of clean air, water, environmental protection, controlling carbon emissions and expanding advanced renewable energy.

ca_gov_primary_randeep_s_dhillon.quote: I support responsible California crude oil production alongside renewable energy development to stabilize fuel costs, protect jobs, and reduce dependence on foreign energy.

statements.text: California should keep its 2045 carbon neutrality target in law.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa: Says California's AB 1279 mandate for carbon neutrality by 2045 remains binding law and is achievable within an all-of-the-above framework.

statements.raceInsight: The state's long-term climate deadline shapes decisions on energy, transportation, and industry for decades. Voters have different views on whether the deadline is realistic and how much it should guide policy.
statements.policyBackground: Carbon neutrality means that the greenhouse gas emissions released are balanced by an equal amount removed or offset, leaving no net addition to the atmosphere. AB 1279 is a 2022 California law that sets this goal for 2045.

ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa.quote: California’s AB 1279 mandate for carbon neutrality by 2045 remains binding law and is achievable within the all-of-the-above framework.

statements.text: California should ban fracking for oil.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_raji_rab: Says fracking and other exploration must follow the highest scientific standards rather than being banned outright.

statements.raceInsight: Fracking has expanded oil and gas output in recent years and raises concerns about water, air, and land near drilling sites. Voters disagree on whether the practice should be prohibited or allowed under strict rules.
statements.policyBackground: Hydraulic fracturing, or fracking, injects water, sand, and chemicals underground at high pressure to release oil or gas from rock. A ban would prohibit this practice in the state.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: Fracking and other explorations must be in accordance with the highest scientific standards.

statements.text: California should prioritize keeping fuel prices low when planning for gasoline supply.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer: Plans to work with the California Energy Commission to create an "affordability first framework" to avoid future supply shortages and price spikes.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa: He proposes directing the Air Resources Board to set a firm credit price ceiling on the Low-Carbon Fuel Standard to limit how much compliance costs pass through to consumers.

statements.raceInsight: Gasoline prices in California are often well above the national average, and sudden spikes strain household budgets. Voters differ on which factors the state should weigh most when ensuring fuel supply.
statements.policyBackground: The California Energy Commission is the state agency that forecasts energy supply and demand and plans for reliable fuel and power. Supply planning can consider reliability, environmental goals, and cost.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: Over the long-term, I’ll work with the California Energy Commission and other policy leaders to create an “affordability first framework” to avoid future supply shortages and price spikes.

ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa.quote: The Governor can direct CARB to implement a firm credit price ceiling that limits the pass-through of LCFS compliance costs to consumers.

statements.text: Utility companies should be allowed to contribute money to candidates for office.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer: Says he will ban utility contributions to candidates and reform state oversight of utilities.

statements.raceInsight: Utilities are regulated monopolies whose rates are set by state regulators, so their political spending draws attention. Voters want to know whether utility money should be allowed to influence elections.
statements.policyBackground: Utility companies provide services such as electricity, natural gas, or water, and are often regulated by the state. A campaign contribution is money given to support a candidate's election. Candidates for office are people seeking elected positions in government.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: This includes banning utility contributions to candidates and reforming state oversight of utility companies to better serve the people of California.

statements.draft: Utility companies should be banned from contributing money to candidates for office.

statements.text: California should keep its gasoline tax in place.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond: Would pause California's gas tax to provide relief.

statements.raceInsight: California has one of the highest gasoline taxes in the nation, and drivers feel changes at the pump quickly. Voters weigh the short-term relief from a tax pause against the funding that gas tax revenue supports.
statements.policyBackground: A gasoline tax is a per-gallon charge on fuel sold in California, and its revenue is generally used for transportation purposes such as road maintenance. Keeping the tax means not suspending or reducing it. Taxes are compulsory payments collected by government to fund public spending.

ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond.quote: Pause California’s Gas tax to provide relief in the midst of Trump’s Iran War tax

statements.draft: California should pause its gasoline tax.

statements.text: California should support federal plans to open its coast to offshore oil drilling.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa: Opposes President Trump's proposal to open up offshore oil drilling in California.

statements.raceInsight: Offshore drilling would involve federal waters off California's coast, raising concerns about oil spills, tourism, and coastal communities. Voters differ on whether new offshore leasing would bring energy benefits that outweigh these risks.
statements.policyBackground: Offshore oil drilling involves extracting oil from wells in federal waters off the coast. Federal plans can include leasing offshore areas to energy companies, which requires federal decisions. The rewrite describes the position of those who favor state support for such federal leasing.

ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa.quote: I have two words for President Trump’s proposal to open up offshore oil drilling in my state: no way.

statements.draft: California should oppose federal plans to open its coast to offshore oil drilling.

statements.text: California should let the market set prices for Low-Carbon Fuel Standard credits without a cap.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa: Proposes directing the Air Resources Board to implement a firm credit price ceiling on the Low-Carbon Fuel Standard to limit pass-through of compliance costs to consumers.

statements.raceInsight: Fuel programs that add compliance costs can show up in what drivers pay at the pump. Voters weigh the cost to consumers against the climate goals these programs are meant to advance.
statements.policyBackground: The Low-Carbon Fuel Standard is a state program that requires fuel producers to reduce the carbon intensity of their fuels, and companies can buy and sell credits to meet those requirements. A price cap would set a maximum price that credits could reach. The rewrite describes the position of those who oppose capping credit prices.

ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa.quote: The Governor can direct CARB to implement a firm credit price ceiling that limits the pass-through of LCFS compliance costs to consumers.

statements.draft: California should cap the price of credits under its Low-Carbon Fuel Standard.

statements.text: California should reopen power plants that were closed.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri: Would reopen power plants closed under green energy policies, starting with San Onofre Generating Station.

statements.raceInsight: Decisions about which power plants stay open affect electricity supply, costs, and emissions. Voters have different views on whether closed plants should return to service to support reliability.
statements.policyBackground: A power plant is a facility that generates electricity, and closures often happen when operators or regulators decide a facility is no longer needed or economical. Reopening a closed plant would require approvals and may involve safety and environmental review.

ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri.quote: We will re-open all power plants that have closed down due to green new policies, starting with San Onofre Generating Station.

statements.text: California should increase the supply of affordable housing.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_akinyemi_agbede: Supports expanding access to affordable housing while enhancing support services for homeless individuals.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_erin_zez_zezulak: Says she would maximize California's cities to enable affordable housing for all.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra: On his first day as governor, he will declare California's housing shortage a state of emergency and make housing production the paramount priority.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell: Aims to stabilize rents, expand housing supply, and lower monthly housing costs.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan: Plans to drive down the cost of living and build more affordable housing.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_katie_porter: Porter plans to speed up housing construction by nearly two years and enforce housing laws to ensure prompt certificates of occupancy.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_satish_rao: Supports continuing recent CEQA reforms that address abuses blocking housing, with monitoring.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer: Steyer says California must build every type of home, from shelters and transitional housing to apartments, starter homes, and single-family homes.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond: Would build 2 million affordable housing units using surplus property owned by school districts in each of the 58 counties.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_gretha_solorzano: The plan aims to tackle California's housing shortage.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_ramsey_robinson: Supports guaranteed housing with costs capped at 20% of income.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_serge_fiankan: Serge Fiankan plans to streamline building permits and reduce construction costs to expand housing.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri: He would expand Section 8 housing to help banks relinquish vacant property to move homeless people off the street.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz: He would build millions of $10,000 movable tiny homes and seek to use unused commercial or housing space.

statements.raceInsight: Housing costs are a major concern for many Californians, including renters and people trying to buy their first home. Voters often weigh how much the state should do to add lower-cost homes compared with other priorities.
statements.policyBackground: Affordable housing refers to homes priced so that households with moderate or lower incomes can pay for them without strain. Increasing supply means building or making more of these homes available over time.

ca_gov_primary_akinyemi_agbede.quote: Expanding access to affordable housing while enhancing support services for homeless individuals, ensuring stable living conditions and long-term solutions.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: On my first day as Governor, I will issue an executive order declaring California’s housing shortage a state of emergency and directing every state agency to treat housing production and affordability as the paramount priority.

ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.quote: Goal: Stabilize rents, expand supply, and lower monthly costs.

ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.quote: He will work to drive down the cost of living, build more affordable housing, make our cities safe, and ensure all kids have an opportunity to succeed.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: I have a plan to speed up building by nearly two years, putting California on par with its peer states that also have worker and environmental protections. This will bring down the costs of apartment housing by 20%.

ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.quote: There has been recent progress (e.g., CEQA abuses that prevent housing from being built), but it needs to continue and be monitored.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: We must build every type of home to meet the needs of every Californian: from shelters and transitional housing, to encouraging and supporting the building of apartments and starter homes, as well as single family homes.

ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond.quote: Build 2 million affordable housing units using the surplus property owned by school districts in each of the 58 counties in our state

ca_gov_primary_erin_zez_zezulak.quote: Working with my grandfather, a building contractor, helped me see how to maximize our cities, enabling affordable housing for all.

ca_gov_primary_gretha_solorzano.quote: I will also tackle California's housing shortage, and I will reverse the decline in our education system.

ca_gov_primary_ramsey_robinson.quote: Our socialist campaign demands guaranteed housing capped at 20% of income, free healthcare, free childcare and union jobs at minimum $30/hour with a guaranteed dignified retirement.

ca_gov_primary_serge_fiankan.quote: Streamlined building permits, reduced construction costs, priority housing for essential workers, and affordable/supportive housing options; including tiny homes, modular units, and community-based services to help people stabilize and rebuild.

ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri.quote: I will expand on Section 8 Housing that will help allow banks relinquish vacant property and actually get the homeless off the street were the people will have a better stake in their community.

ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz.quote: HOUSING FOR ALL IN CALIFORNIA AND USA (AS ANYONE CAN DRIVE HERE IN A DAY OR TWO), BUILDING TENS OF MILLIONS OF $10K TINY HOMES WITH WHEELS

statements.text: California should build every type of home, including shelters, apartments, starter homes and single-family homes.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer: Steyer says California must build every type of home, from shelters and transitional housing to apartments, starter homes, and single-family homes.

statements.raceInsight: Californians disagree about what kinds of homes should be built and where, which affects neighborhoods, costs, and access for people at different life stages. Voters often want to know whether the state should focus on one type of housing or many.
statements.policyBackground: Transitional housing is temporary housing that helps people move toward stable homes. Starter homes are smaller, lower-priced homes often bought by first-time buyers, while single-family homes are detached houses for one household.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: We must build every type of home to meet the needs of every Californian: from shelters and transitional housing, to encouraging and supporting the building of apartments and starter homes, as well as single family homes.

statements.text: The state should put vacant buildings and unused properties to use as housing.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri: He would expand Section 8 housing to help banks relinquish vacant property to move homeless people off the street.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond: Would build 2 million affordable housing units using surplus property owned by school districts in each of the 58 counties.

statements.raceInsight: Empty commercial buildings and vacant properties exist alongside high housing costs and visible homelessness in many California communities. Voters may differ on whether reusing existing buildings is a faster or cheaper path than new construction.
