statements.policyBackground: Converting a building means changing its use, such as turning an office into apartments. Section 8 is a federal rental assistance program that helps eligible low-income households pay rent to private landlords.

ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond.quote: Build 2 million affordable housing units using the surplus property owned by school districts in each of the 58 counties in our state

ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri.quote: I will expand on Section 8 Housing that will help allow banks relinquish vacant property and actually get the homeless off the street were the people will have a better stake in their community.

statements.text: California should reduce government regulations that slow down housing construction.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_katie_porter: Porter plans to speed up housing construction by nearly two years and enforce housing laws to ensure prompt certificates of occupancy.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_serge_fiankan: Serge Fiankan plans to streamline building permits and reduce construction costs to expand housing.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_steve_hilton: Hilton proposed a ballot initiative to bar private lawsuits under the California Environmental Quality Act, a process that can slow housing construction.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_max_fomin: Max Fomin says he will cut red tape that raises housing costs.

statements.raceInsight: The time and cost of permits and approvals are often cited as reasons housing takes years to finish. Voters differ on how much government review is needed to protect safety, the environment, and local planning goals.
statements.policyBackground: Building permits are approvals from local governments required before construction. A certificate of occupancy is the official document confirming a building is safe to live in, and it is needed before residents can move in.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: I have a plan to speed up building by nearly two years, putting California on par with its peer states that also have worker and environmental protections. This will bring down the costs of apartment housing by 20%.

ca_gov_primary_steve_hilton.quote: The measure would prohibit private lawsuits related to the California Environmental Quality Act and cap impact fees paid by homebuilders and developers.

ca_gov_primary_serge_fiankan.quote: Streamlined building permits, reduced construction costs, priority housing for essential workers, and affordable/supportive housing options; including tiny homes, modular units, and community-based services to help people stabilize and rebuild.

ca_gov_primary_max_fomin.quote: I will tackle the “California Tax” on everyday life. From freezing utility rate hikes to cutting the red tape that makes housing so expensive.

statements.text: Local governments should be allowed to adopt rent control within statewide rules.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra: He will fully enforce the Tenant Protection Act and support local rent control within the statewide framework.

statements.raceInsight: Rent levels affect the majority of Californians, who rent their homes. Voters often disagree on whether limits on rent increases protect tenants or reduce the supply of rental housing over time.
statements.policyBackground: Rent control is a local rule that limits how much a landlord can raise rent, often on existing tenants. The Tenant Protection Act is a California state law that sets statewide limits on rent increases and reasons for evictions.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: I will enforce those protections fully and stand behind communities that have chosen to protect renters through local rent control, within the statewide framework that keeps housing construction moving forward.

statements.text: The state should freeze rents for a period of time.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz: He would impose a rent freeze.

statements.raceInsight: Rising rents are a central concern for renters across California. Voters differ on whether a temporary freeze would give households relief or limit landlords' ability to cover costs.
statements.policyBackground: A rent freeze keeps rents from rising above their current level for a set period. It is a stronger measure than rent control, which usually allows limited annual increases.

ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz.quote: RENT FREEZE! RENTS HAVE GONE UP ASTRONOMICALLY IN THE PAST 2 DECADES, FAR OUTPACING WAGES.

statements.text: California should change environmental review rules under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) to speed up housing projects.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_satish_rao: Supports continuing recent CEQA reforms that address abuses blocking housing, with monitoring.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_steve_hilton: Hilton proposed a ballot initiative that would bar private lawsuits under the California Environmental Quality Act and cap impact fees paid by homebuilders and developers.

statements.raceInsight: Environmental review is one of the most debated tools in California housing policy. Voters weigh faster approvals for homes against concerns about environmental protection and community input.
statements.policyBackground: The California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) requires state and local agencies to study the environmental effects of many projects before approving them. Private lawsuits are one way groups can challenge these reviews.

ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.quote: There has been recent progress (e.g., CEQA abuses that prevent housing from being built), but it needs to continue and be monitored.

ca_gov_primary_steve_hilton.quote: The measure would prohibit private lawsuits related to the California Environmental Quality Act and cap impact fees paid by homebuilders and developers.

statements.text: Local governments should be free to set the impact fees that homebuilders pay.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_steve_hilton: Hilton proposed a ballot initiative that would bar private lawsuits under the California Environmental Quality Act and cap impact fees paid by homebuilders and developers.

statements.raceInsight: Fees charged on new development are part of the cost of building homes, and they can be passed on to buyers and renters. Voters differ on whether these fees pay for needed local services or add to housing prices.
statements.policyBackground: Impact fees are charges that developers pay to local governments to help cover the public costs of new construction, such as roads, schools, and utilities. A cap would set a maximum limit on these fees. The rewrite describes the position of those who oppose state limits on local fee-setting.

ca_gov_primary_steve_hilton.quote: The measure would prohibit private lawsuits related to the California Environmental Quality Act and cap impact fees paid by homebuilders and developers.

statements.draft: California should cap the impact fees that homebuilders pay to local governments.

statements.text: The state should provide down payment assistance to help people buy their first homes.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra: He will expand California's down payment assistance program, increase its funding, and broaden eligibility.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond: Would provide down payment assistance grants for first-time home buyers.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_raji_rab: Plans to seek federal funding and offer housing plans to ease down payment, mortgage, rent and utility costs.

statements.raceInsight: Saving for a down payment is one of the largest obstacles to homeownership in California's high-priced market. Voters often weigh whether public help for buyers is a good use of state funds compared with other housing approaches.
statements.policyBackground: A down payment is the upfront share of a home's price paid by the buyer, with the rest usually financed by a mortgage. Down payment assistance programs provide funds or grants to help eligible buyers cover this cost.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: I will expand California’s down payment assistance program, increase its funding, and broaden eligibility so more first-time buyers can access it faster.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I will seek federal funding to ease burdensome complexities and offer real housing plans to ease down payment, mortgage, rent and utilities.

ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond.quote: Provide down payment assistance grants for first-time home buyers

statements.topic: Penalties for Cities Missing Housing Goals
statements.text: The state should impose financial penalties on cities that fail to meet their state-required housing plans.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra: He will direct HCD to identify cities failing their housing element commitments and begin enforcement, including financial penalties where appropriate.

statements.raceInsight: Whether cities meet state housing targets affects where and how many homes get built across California. Voters often disagree on how much the state should push local governments compared with leaving decisions to cities.
statements.policyBackground: Each city and county must adopt a housing element, a plan showing how it will meet its share of the state's housing needs. HCD, the state Department of Housing and Community Development, reviews these plans and can take enforcement steps when they are not followed.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: I will direct the California Department of Housing and Community Development to immediately identify cities reneging on their housing element commitments and commence enforcement action, including financial penalties where appropriate.

statements.text: School districts should keep their surplus land for school use rather than using it for affordable housing.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond: Would build 2 million affordable housing units using surplus property owned by school districts in each of the 58 counties.

statements.raceInsight: Public land that is no longer needed for schools could be a source of sites for homes in communities with few available parcels. Voters often consider whether using such land for housing is a good fit with school district needs.
statements.policyBackground: Surplus land is property a school district owns that it no longer needs for its current purposes. School districts are local public agencies that operate public schools. Affordable housing refers to homes priced below market rates for lower-income households.

ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond.quote: Build 2 million affordable housing units using the surplus property owned by school districts in each of the 58 counties in our state

statements.draft: The state should use surplus land owned by school districts to build affordable housing.

statements.text: California should not borrow $10 billion through bonds to fund affordable housing construction.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond: Would secure a $10 billion housing bond to build affordable housing.

statements.raceInsight: Bonds are a major way California pays for large public projects, and they are repaid by taxpayers over time. Voters weigh the cost of borrowing against the need for more affordable homes.
statements.policyBackground: A state bond is a form of borrowing in which the state sells debt to investors and repays it over time, typically with interest. Affordable housing refers to homes priced below market rates so that lower-income households can afford them. Construction funding would pay for building new housing units.

ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond.quote: Secure a $10 billion housing bond to build affordable housing

statements.draft: California should issue a $10 billion bond to fund affordable housing construction.

statements.topic: Housing Costs Capped at 20% of Income
statements.text: The state should not set a limit on housing costs as a share of household income.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_ramsey_robinson: Supports guaranteed housing with costs capped at 20% of income.

statements.raceInsight: Many households spend more than a third of their income on housing, which limits savings and other spending. Voters differ on whether government should guarantee a cost limit or leave housing prices to the market.
statements.policyBackground: Housing costs as a share of income is the portion of a household's earnings spent on rent or mortgage payments. A state guarantee would set a maximum share, such as 20 percent, that housing should not exceed. The rewrite describes the position of those who oppose such a state-set limit.

ca_gov_primary_ramsey_robinson.quote: Our socialist campaign demands guaranteed housing capped at 20% of income, free healthcare, free childcare and union jobs at minimum $30/hour with a guaranteed dignified retirement.

statements.draft: The state should guarantee housing that costs no more than 20% of a household's income.

statements.text: People experiencing homelessness should be required to accept treatment to receive housing.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_serge_fiankan: Serge Fiankan states no one will be required to accept treatment to receive housing.

statements.raceInsight: Voters differ on whether housing assistance should come with conditions such as treatment. This question affects who gets housing and how programs are designed across the state's large homeless population.
statements.policyBackground: Some programs require participation in treatment, such as for addiction or mental illness, as a condition of staying in housing or receiving services. Other programs offer housing without requiring treatment, which is often called a housing-first approach. The statement asks whether treatment should be a condition of receiving housing.

ca_gov_primary_serge_fiankan.quote: No. The plan explicitly states no one will be required to accept treatment to receive housing.

statements.text: Local governments should clear unsafe street encampments.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_max_fomin: Max Fomin says he will fix the mental health system and clear encampments with humane but strong enforcement.

statements.raceInsight: Tent encampments are visible in many California cities and raise concerns about public safety, sanitation, and the health of the people living in them. How governments respond to encampments is a major local and statewide debate.
statements.policyBackground: An encampment is a group of tents or structures on public land where people live without permanent housing. Clearing an encampment means removing people and belongings from the site, often with notice and offers of shelter or services. Critics raise concerns about where displaced people go, while supporters argue removal is needed for safety.

ca_gov_primary_elaine_culotti.quote: End unsafe street encampments, prosecute crime, and treat first responders as essential heroes.

ca_gov_primary_max_fomin.quote: We will fix our mental health system, clear the encampments with humane but strong enforcement, and ensure every tax dollar is audited for results.

statements.text: The state should fund mental health treatment as part of addressing homelessness.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_elaine_culotti: Would fund proven mental health treatment and practical housing solutions.

statements.raceInsight: Many people who are homeless also live with serious mental illness, so the level of mental health funding affects how the state's homelessness response works. Voters will compare how much weight to give mental health services versus other tools.
statements.policyBackground: Mental health treatment includes therapy, psychiatric care, medication management, and crisis services. Funding for these services can be provided through state budgets, grants to counties, or Medi-Cal coverage. Supporters argue treatment helps people stabilize and keep housing.

ca_gov_primary_elaine_culotti.quote: Health and Safety that funds proven mental health treatment, practical housing solutions, and accountable public safety.

statements.text: Preventing homelessness should be a top priority in state spending on homelessness.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_katie_porter: Porter's homelessness plan focuses on homeless prevention through emergency rental assistance and rapid re-housing, plus interim housing.

statements.raceInsight: Rising rents and housing costs push many families to the brink of losing their homes, so the choice between preventing homelessness and responding after it happens shapes how the state spends its money. Voters will consider how to balance prevention with services for people already on the streets.
statements.policyBackground: Homelessness prevention provides help such as rental assistance or other support to keep people in their homes before they lose them. Rapid re-housing moves people who are already homeless into apartments quickly, often with short-term rent help. Critics of a prevention focus argue that resources are needed for people already living outside.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: My homelessness plan focuses on two strategies that California has not adopted: homeless prevention through emergency rental assistance and rapid re-housing, and interim housing that can keep people from being unsheltered, which is itself a risk factor for mental health and substance use problems.

statements.text: State homelessness spending should require measurable results before more money is added.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_chad_bianco: He will demand real results for the billions spent on homelessness and end spending without accountability.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra: He will establish a dedicated, stable funding stream for homelessness prevention tied to measurable reduction targets.

statements.raceInsight: California has spent billions of dollars on homelessness over recent years, and many voters question whether those funds have produced visible results. How the state measures success will shape future budgets.
statements.policyBackground: Performance-based spending ties funding to measurable outcomes, such as the number of people placed in housing or how many remain housed. Supporters say it makes programs more effective, while others caution that some results take years to appear or are hard to measure.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: As Governor, I would establish a dedicated, stable targeted homelessness prevention funding stream within the state’s homelessness response, one that communities can plan around year over year, tied to measurable reduction targets and local investment.

ca_gov_primary_chad_bianco.quote: I will demand real results for the billions spent on homelessness, and end the cycle of spending without accountability.

statements.text: The state should quickly build emergency housing where people can spend nights indoors with access to care.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer: Steyer says he will conduct a full spending review and quickly build emergency housing so people can spend nights indoors with access to care.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan: In 2022, decreased funds for affordable housing to prioritize shelter construction, quick-build communities, and temporary housing.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_katie_porter: Porter's homelessness plan includes interim housing alongside emergency rental assistance and rapid re-housing.

statements.raceInsight: Visible homelessness on sidewalks and in parks makes the speed of getting people indoors a central concern for many Californians. Voters will weigh how quickly the state should expand emergency shelter capacity.
statements.policyBackground: Emergency housing includes shelters, quick-build cabins, and temporary units that offer short-term places to stay, often with supportive services. Quick-build projects use prefabricated or simplified construction to open sites faster than traditional developments. Debate centers on cost, location, and whether temporary units lead to permanent housing.

ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.quote: In 2022, Mahan decreased the funds made available to affordable housing to prioritize shelter construction, quick-build communities, and temporary housing.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: My homelessness plan focuses on two strategies that California has not adopted: homeless prevention through emergency rental assistance and rapid re-housing, and interim housing that can keep people from being unsheltered, which is itself a risk factor for mental health and substance use problems.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: As Governor, I will conduct a full spending review, partner with local governments to identify and implement approaches that work across all levels of need, and quickly build emergency housing so people on the street can spend the night indoors with access to care.

statements.topic: Measure E funding shift to shelters
statements.text: Funding from local housing measures should remain dedicated to permanent affordable housing and not be used for shelters or temporary housing.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan: In 2022 decreased funds for affordable housing to prioritize shelter construction, quick-build communities, and temporary housing.

statements.raceInsight: Local housing funds are limited, so choices about whether to prioritize long-term affordable housing or short-term shelter affect how cities respond to homelessness. Voters in areas with such measures face this trade-off directly.
statements.policyBackground: Local housing measures are typically local taxes or bonds approved by voters to fund housing programs. Shelters provide short-term emergency housing, while temporary housing is a broader category that includes transitional or interim living arrangements.

ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.quote: In 2022, Mahan decreased the funds made available to affordable housing to prioritize shelter construction, quick-build communities, and temporary housing.

statements.draft: Funding from local housing measures should shift from affordable housing to shelters and temporary housing.

statements.topic: Rescue Ranch as a homelessness solution
statements.text: Government should not rely on the Rescue Ranch program as a solution to homelessness.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_raji_rab: Supports Rescue Ranch as a practical solution to homelessness.

statements.raceInsight: Voters look at specific programs when judging how to address homelessness, and support for particular models shapes which approaches receive public funding. Each program's results will be part of the broader debate.
statements.policyBackground: The Rescue Ranch program is a named initiative whose specific design and goals are described in its own program materials, which are not included here. Homelessness refers to people lacking a regular, adequate place to live. The statement concerns whether this particular program should be used as a government response to homelessness.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I support Rescue Ranch as a practical solution to address homelessness and meet the essential needs of individuals seeking help.

statements.draft: Government should support the Rescue Ranch program as a solution to homelessness.

statements.text: Retailers should set their consumer prices without a legal requirement to pass wholesale cost decreases on to customers.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell: Proposes a mandatory pass-through of wholesale cost drops to consumers.

statements.raceInsight: Grocery and retail prices affect nearly every household, and voters care whether savings reach shoppers when a store's own costs fall. This question addresses how price changes flow from suppliers to the checkout line.
statements.policyBackground: Wholesale cost is the price a retailer pays a supplier for goods before marking them up for sale. Passing cost decreases on to consumers means lowering retail prices when the retailer's own costs fall.

ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.quote: Mandatory pass‑through of wholesale cost drops

statements.draft: Retailers should be required to pass wholesale cost decreases on to consumers.

statements.text: Retailers should not be required to disclose how much of a product's price is due to tariffs.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa: Proposes legislation requiring all retailers to display Tariff Impact Labels showing how much of a product's price is attributable to tariffs.

statements.raceInsight: Tariffs on imported goods can raise prices on everyday products, and shoppers often cannot see how much of a price comes from them. Voters are weighing whether they want clearer information about this cost at the store.
statements.policyBackground: Tariffs are taxes charged on imported goods, and they can be passed on to consumers through higher retail prices. A labeling requirement would have retailers show the portion of a price attributed to tariffs. The rewrite describes the position of those who oppose such a requirement.

ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa.quote: Enact legislation requiring all retailers to display “Tariff Impact Labels” showing how much of a product’s price is attributable to tariffs, similar to gas pump stickers showing tax components.

statements.draft: Retailers should be required to display labels showing how much of a product's price is due to tariffs.

statements.text: The state should increase the building of affordable housing.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan: Plans to drive down the cost of living, build more affordable housing, make cities safe, and ensure all kids have an opportunity to succeed.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_akinyemi_agbede: Supports expanding access to affordable housing.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra: On his first day as governor, he will declare California's housing shortage a state of emergency and make housing production the paramount priority.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell: Aims to stabilize rents, expand housing supply, and lower monthly housing costs.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer: Steyer says California must build every type of home, from shelters and transitional housing to apartments, starter homes, and single-family homes.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond: Would secure a $10 billion housing bond to build affordable housing.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_erin_zez_zezulak: Says she would maximize California's cities to enable affordable housing for all.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_gretha_solorzano: The plan aims to tackle California's housing shortage.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_ramsey_robinson: Supports guaranteed housing with costs capped at 20% of income.

statements.raceInsight: Housing costs are among the largest expenses for California households, and many residents report difficulty finding homes they can afford. How the state approaches building new housing is a major part of the state's cost-of-living debate.
statements.policyBackground: Affordable housing refers to homes priced so that lower- and middle-income households can pay for them without excessive strain. State efforts to increase it can include funding, zoning changes, or incentives for construction. Debate often centers on how much public involvement is appropriate and how to pay for it.

ca_gov_primary_akinyemi_agbede.quote: Expanding access to affordable housing while enhancing support services for homeless individuals, ensuring stable living conditions and long-term solutions.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: On my first day as Governor, I will issue an executive order declaring California’s housing shortage a state of emergency and directing every state agency to treat housing production and affordability as the paramount priority.

ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.quote: Goal: Stabilize rents, expand supply, and lower monthly costs.

ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.quote: He will work to drive down the cost of living, build more affordable housing, make our cities safe, and ensure all kids have an opportunity to succeed.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: We must build every type of home to meet the needs of every Californian: from shelters and transitional housing, to encouraging and supporting the building of apartments and starter homes, as well as single family homes.

ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond.quote: Secure a $10 billion housing bond to build affordable housing

ca_gov_primary_erin_zez_zezulak.quote: Working with my grandfather, a building contractor, helped me see how to maximize our cities, enabling affordable housing for all.

ca_gov_primary_gretha_solorzano.quote: I will also tackle California's housing shortage, and I will reverse the decline in our education system.

ca_gov_primary_ramsey_robinson.quote: Our socialist campaign demands guaranteed housing capped at 20% of income, free healthcare, free childcare and union jobs at minimum $30/hour with a guaranteed dignified retirement.

statements.text: The state should offer child care to all families at no cost.
statements.raceInsight: Child care costs are a major expense for working families in California, and access affects whether parents can stay in the workforce. Voters often weigh how much the state should pay for child care compared with what families pay directly.
statements.policyBackground: Child care refers to supervised care for young children while parents work or study. Universal programs make care available to all families regardless of income, and they can be funded through public spending, with or without fees charged to parents.

ca_gov_primary_ramsey_robinson.quote: Our socialist campaign demands guaranteed housing capped at 20% of income, free healthcare, free childcare and union jobs at minimum $30/hour with a guaranteed dignified retirement.

statements.text: California should make tuition free at public colleges and universities for students.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_katie_porter: Would make college tuition-free for all Californians by pairing community college with two free years at UC and CSU.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond: Would launch a pilot program for a free 4-year degree at the CSU or UC.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_satish_rao: Opposes mandating free tuition for the largely wealthy student population at Berkeley.

statements.raceInsight: College costs affect whether students can enroll, finish degrees, and avoid debt. Voters differ on whether tuition should be waived broadly, targeted to some students, or kept as it is.
statements.policyBackground: Tuition is the fee charged for instruction at public colleges such as community colleges, the California State University (CSU) system, and the University of California (UC) system. Free tuition programs cover some or all of these charges, and they may apply to all students or only to selected groups or pilot programs.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: As Governor, I will fulfill the forgotten promise of our state: tuition-free college for all Californians. By pairing two years of free community college, which already exists through the California College Promise, with two free years at our UC and CSU campuses, we will create a pathway for a four-year degree tuition-free.

ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.quote: Simply mandating “free tuition” for the largely wealthy student population at Berkeley would amount to a massive financial handout to people who don’t need it.

ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond.quote: Launch a pilot program for a free 4-year degree at the CSU or UC

statements.text: California should set a goal that every public school student can read by third grade.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond: Would lead a 5-year plan to ensure every California student can read by third grade.

statements.raceInsight: Reading skills in the early grades affect students' later success in every subject. Voters often disagree about which state actions are most effective in reaching this goal.
statements.policyBackground: Third grade is widely used as a checkpoint for reading ability because students shift from learning to read to reading to learn. A statewide goal sets a target for schools, and plans to meet it can include training, materials, and timelines.

ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond.quote: Lead a 5-year plan to ensure every California student can read by third grade

statements.text: California should increase state funding for public K-12 schools.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond: Supports finally fully funding public schools.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa: Says he made record investments in public schools, including the largest single allocation of school safety funds in state history.

statements.raceInsight: State funding is the largest source of revenue for California's K-12 schools and shapes class sizes, staffing, and programs. Voters often weigh how much the state should spend on schools against other budget priorities.
statements.policyBackground: K-12 school funding in California comes from state and local sources and is distributed to districts largely on a per-student basis. Increasing funding means the state provides more money to school districts for operations and programs.

ca_gov_primary_tony_k_thurmond.quote: That's why he's fighting for a tax on billionaires, healthcare for all, abolishing ICE, 2 million new units of housing, finally fully funding our public schools, abortion care that is legal and accessible, getting weapons of war off of our streets, and protecting democracy.

ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa.quote: Made record investments in public schools, including the largest single allocation of school safety funds in state history

statements.text: The state should not cancel student loan debt for borrowers and should require full repayment.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_raji_rab: Says student debt must be deleted.

statements.raceInsight: Student loan balances affect graduates' finances, home buying, and career choices. Voters disagree on whether debt should be forgiven and who should pay for it.
statements.policyBackground: Student loan debt is money borrowed to pay for education that must be repaid, usually with interest. Cancellation means forgiving some or all of the remaining balance so the borrower no longer owes it. The statement concerns whether borrowers should be required to repay their loans in full.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: Student debt must be deleted. Party politics has scorched us, setting divisions in our democracy.

statements.draft: The state should cancel student loan debt for borrowers.

statements.text: The state should not fund free meals for all public school students.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer: Says universal healthy school meals will be funded year-round.

statements.raceInsight: School meals affect children's nutrition and can ease household food costs. Voters differ on whether free meals should be offered to every student and on how long the program should run each year.
statements.policyBackground: Free meals are food provided to students at no cost to their families. State funding means money from the state budget used to pay for a program. Summer meals refer to food programs that serve children when schools are not in session.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: We will ensure universal healthy school meals are funded year-round.

statements.draft: The state should fund healthy meals for all public school students, including during the summer.

statements.text: Teachers' unions should have a role in collective bargaining over teacher contracts.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri: Would abolish the California Teachers Association's collective bargaining role.

statements.raceInsight: Teacher contracts set salaries, working conditions, and job protections that affect schools across the state. Voters differ on whether teachers' unions should negotiate these terms on behalf of educators.
statements.policyBackground: Collective bargaining is the process in which employee representatives negotiate contracts with an employer, in this case school districts. The California Teachers Association is the state's largest teachers' union and takes part in these negotiations.

ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri.quote: Abolish the CTA for ‘collective bargaining.’

statements.topic: Funding for private and home school students
statements.text: State education funding should follow students to private, religious, or home schools.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz: Would pay parents who send children to private, religious, or home schools the per-child public school amount, currently $25,000.

statements.raceInsight: Public school funding is tied to students, so decisions about where that money goes affect both public schools and families' education choices. Voters often disagree on whether public money should support schooling outside the public system.
statements.policyBackground: Per-student funding is the amount of public money allocated for each enrolled student. Education choice programs use this amount to pay for tuition or other costs at schools outside the traditional public system.

ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz.quote: IF PARENTS WANT TO SEND THEIR KIDS TO PRIVATE OR RELIGIOUS SCHOOLS, OR HOME-SCHOOL, THEY'LL GET A YEARLY PAYMENT OF WHAT THE PUBLIC SCHOOLS SPEND PER CHILD (EXCLUDING CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS), CURRENTLY $25,000.

statements.text: California should not restrict pesticide use in food served in schools.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz: He would ban sugar, pesticides, and chemicals from school food.

statements.raceInsight: Parents, school nutrition staff, and farmers all have a stake in what ends up on school plates. Voters often weigh food safety and health concerns against cost, sourcing, and how much rules should govern school meal providers.
statements.policyBackground: Pesticides are chemicals used to control insects, weeds, and other pests on crops, and residues can remain on food. School food rules set standards for meals served to students. The policy question is whether state rules would limit pesticide or chemical use in that food.

ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz.quote: BAN SUGAR, PESTICIDES AND CHEMICALS FROM SCHOOL FOOD.

statements.draft: California should ban pesticides and chemicals from school food.

statements.text: California should not restrict sugar in food served in schools and should leave those choices to local districts.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz: He would ban sugar, pesticides, and chemicals from school food.

statements.raceInsight: School meals and snacks are a daily part of children's diets, so rules on sugar affect many families. Voters may have different views on how much the state should limit what schools serve compared with what parents and districts decide.
statements.policyBackground: School food rules set standards for meals and snacks served to students, often in public schools that receive federal nutrition funding. Sugar content is one factor these standards may address. Leaving choices to local districts means each district decides its own food policies.

ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz.quote: BAN SUGAR, PESTICIDES AND CHEMICALS FROM SCHOOL FOOD.

statements.draft: California should ban sugar from school food.

statements.text: California should ban the sale of assault weapons.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_eric_swalwell: In 2019 made gun control a signature campaign issue, including a mandatory buyback of assault weapons and universal background checks.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa: Says he led efforts to pass a landmark assault weapons ban in California.

statements.raceInsight: Gun violence and mass shootings are a major concern for many Californians, and the state's rules on which firearms can be sold directly affect communities across the state. Voters often look to the governor's position on weapons policy when judging how the state will handle public safety.
statements.policyBackground: An assault weapons ban restricts the sale of certain semiautomatic rifles and related firearms, usually defined by their features and design. Supporters see it as a way to limit weapons designed for rapid fire, while opponents argue it restricts lawful gun ownership and that the features it targets do not drive gun crime. Some versions also address firearms already owned, through registration or buyback programs.

ca_gov_primary_eric_swalwell.quote: In 2019, Swalwell made gun control a signature issue of his presidential campaign, including a ban with a mandatory buyback of all firearms deemed assault weapons, and universal background checks.

ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa.quote: Led efforts to pass landmark assault weapons ban in California

statements.text: Background checks should be required for all gun purchases.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_eric_swalwell: In 2019 made gun control a signature campaign issue, including a mandatory buyback of assault weapons and universal background checks.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_raji_rab: Supports strict background checks and stronger gun violence laws while stating support for the Second Amendment.

statements.raceInsight: Background checks are one of the most widely discussed gun policies in California, and they affect how easily residents can buy firearms from private sellers or at gun shows. Voters weigh how these checks balance public safety with gun ownership rights.
statements.policyBackground: A background check is a review of a buyer's criminal and mental health records before a gun sale is completed. Universal background checks would apply this review to all gun sales, including private sales, not only sales by licensed dealers. Supporters say it closes gaps in the system, while opponents raise concerns about record-keeping and the burden on private sellers.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I am the greatest supporter of constitutional rights including 2nd amendment. However, I will not let that overtake public safety. I will enforce strict measures and background checks to prevent deadly weapons in wrong hands.

ca_gov_primary_eric_swalwell.quote: In 2019, Swalwell made gun control a signature issue of his presidential campaign, including a ban with a mandatory buyback of all firearms deemed assault weapons, and universal background checks.

statements.text: Lawful adults should be required to obtain a concealed carry permit before carrying a concealed firearm.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri: Says concealed carry permits are unconstitutional and would work to change requirements so lawful citizens can conceal and carry immediately after purchase and a background cool-down period.

statements.raceInsight: Rules on carrying concealed guns in public shape how Californians protect themselves and how police enforce gun laws. The state's permit process is a central point of debate between gun rights advocates and public safety groups.
statements.policyBackground: A concealed firearm is a handgun or other firearm carried in a way that is hidden from public view. A concealed carry permit is a government-issued authorization, typically requiring background checks and training, that allows a person to carry such a firearm. This statement concerns whether the permit requirement should apply to lawful adults.

ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri.quote: CCW’s are un-Constitutional and will work tirelessly to change the requirements for lawful citizens to ‘conceal and carry’ immediately after purchase and background cool down period so communities can have greater involvement preventing criminal activities.

statements.draft: Lawful adults should be able to carry a concealed firearm without a concealed carry permit.

statements.text: Firearms sold in California should not be required to include an approved trigger lock.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa: Says he required all firearms sold in California to include approved safety trigger locks.

statements.raceInsight: Safe storage rules affect households with children and people living with firearms at home. Voters care about how these design requirements affect both accident prevention and the cost and convenience of owning a gun.
statements.policyBackground: A trigger lock is a device that blocks a firearm's trigger from being pulled. Approved means the device meets a standard set by the state. Firearms are guns sold through retail or private transactions.

ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa.quote: Required all firearms sold in California to include approved safety trigger locks

statements.draft: All firearms sold in California should include an approved trigger lock.

statements.text: California should ban the sale of low-cost handguns, sometimes called Saturday Night Specials.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa: Says he banned cheap handguns known as "Saturday Night Specials."

statements.raceInsight: Restrictions on inexpensive handguns affect which firearms are available to buyers at different income levels. Voters weigh whether such limits reduce gun crime or restrict lawful access to firearms for self-defense.
statements.policyBackground: "Saturday Night Special" is an informal term for small, inexpensive handguns often linked to crime because they are cheap and easy to conceal. Some states and cities have restricted or banned such handguns by setting standards for price, size, or materials. Opponents argue these standards are arbitrary and limit lower-cost options for lawful buyers.

ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa.quote: Banned cheap handguns, called “Saturday Night Specials” that put multiple gun factories in California out of business

statements.text: California should tax drivers based on the number of miles they drive.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_max_fomin: Says he will veto California's mileage tax.

statements.raceInsight: Californians pay gas taxes that fund roads, and as cars become more fuel-efficient and electric, that revenue is shrinking. How the state replaces it affects every driver's costs.
statements.policyBackground: A mileage tax would charge drivers a fee for each mile driven instead of, or in addition to, a tax on fuel. Supporters see it as a way to keep road funding steady as vehicles use less gasoline. Opponents raise concerns about privacy, cost, and how the tax would be collected.

ca_gov_primary_max_fomin.quote: Will veto California’s milage tax, suffocate homelessness, assassinate unemployment, nuke crime, house the unhoused, prosecute statewide corruption, invest in profitable industries, will investigate Veil of Secrecy bill, will retire SB947 & Prop 36, like my coffee iced out.

statements.text: California should raise taxes to pay for transportation projects.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_joseph_cabrera: Argues that the state should not raise taxes for transportation because about $30.1 billion in voter-approved bond money is unspent.

statements.raceInsight: Roads, bridges, and transit are costly to build and maintain, and voters decide how much to pay for them through taxes and bonds. Whether to raise new money or use money already approved is a central question for the state budget.
statements.policyBackground: Transportation projects in California are funded through a mix of taxes, fees, federal money, and bonds. Bonds are loans the state repays over time, and voters must approve them before they can be spent. Unspent bond money is money that has been approved but not yet used for projects.

ca_gov_primary_joseph_cabrera.quote: Sacramento politicians are asking for new taxes, but their own budget—Schedule 11—shows they are sitting on $30.1 billion in unspent, voter-approved bond money. We have nearly $500 million for traffic reduction sitting idle since 2006.

statements.text: California should fund large-scale high-speed rail construction.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_serge_fiankan: Opposes oversized high-speed rail projects that drain resources without delivering results.

statements.raceInsight: High-speed rail is one of the largest public works plans in state history, and its cost and timeline have drawn ongoing attention. Voters weigh how much state money such projects should receive compared with other transportation needs.
statements.policyBackground: High-speed rail would connect California cities with trains that travel at high speeds on dedicated tracks. Large-scale construction requires many years and billions of dollars in public funds. Supporters point to long-term travel and environmental benefits, while critics question cost overruns and delays.

ca_gov_primary_serge_fiankan.quote: No oversized high-speed rail projects that drain resources without delivering results.

statements.text: California should allow autonomous vehicles to control driving without a human ready to take over.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz: Would ban autonomous self-driving vehicles from controlling driving unless an accident is imminent.

statements.raceInsight: Self-driving cars are being tested on California roads, and state rules will shape how quickly they spread. Voters weigh the promise of safer, more convenient travel against concerns about safety and liability.
statements.policyBackground: Autonomous vehicles use sensors and software to steer, brake, and accelerate without a human driver actively controlling them. Some states allow them to operate on public roads with varying oversight. Debate centers on safety testing, who is responsible in a crash, and when a human must be able to take control.

ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz.quote: BAN KILLER SELF-DRIVING VEHICLES FROM CONTROLLING DRIVING UNLESS ACCIDENT IS IMMINENT, AND BAN REMOTE-CONTROLLED VEHICLES!

statements.text: California should allow vehicles to be operated remotely by a person from a distance.
statements.raceInsight: Remote operation of vehicles, such as delivery robots and some automated services, is an emerging use of technology on public roads. Voters must consider how such vehicles fit into existing traffic and safety rules.
statements.policyBackground: Remote operation means a person controls a vehicle from a distant location rather than from inside it. This can be used for delivery or emergency situations. Policy debates focus on whether remote operators can safely respond to road conditions and who is accountable when problems occur.

ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz.quote: BAN KILLER SELF-DRIVING VEHICLES FROM CONTROLLING DRIVING UNLESS ACCIDENT IS IMMINENT, AND BAN REMOTE-CONTROLLED VEHICLES!

statements.text: California should ban voting machines from being used in elections.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri: He would ban voting machines from functioning in California.

statements.raceInsight: How ballots are cast and counted determines whether voters trust the results of elections for governor and every other office. Voters across California hold differing views on whether machines or paper ballots offer the most secure and accurate count.
statements.policyBackground: Voting machines are electronic devices used to mark, tabulate, or count ballots. Some critics question their security and auditability, while election officials generally maintain that they are tested and certified before use.

ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri.quote: Voting machines will be a thing of the past and no longer permitted to function in our state.

statements.text: Voters should reject Proposition 50 on the statewide ballot.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan: Said he would reluctantly support Proposition 50 despite concerns about partisan redistricting.

statements.raceInsight: Ballot measures decided directly by voters can change how California draws its districts for Congress and shape political representation for years. Voters are asked to weigh these changes on their own.
statements.policyBackground: A proposition is a measure placed directly before voters for a statewide decision. The provided source text does not describe the content of Proposition 50, so this background is limited to the term itself.

ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.quote: In 2025, as California’s Proposition 50 (a measure authorizing temporary legislatively drawn congressional maps) headed to the ballot, Mahan criticized Governor Gavin Newsom ’s combative approach to state/national politics and said he would reluctantly support the measure despite concerns about partisan redistricting.

statements.draft: Voters should approve Proposition 50 on the statewide ballot.

statements.text: California should send a mail-in ballot to every registered voter for each election.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_raji_rab: Supports universal mail-in ballots for all registered voters and an independent redistricting process.

statements.raceInsight: Voting by mail affects how easily millions of Californians can take part in elections, and it also shapes how quickly results are counted. Voters have different views on how ballots should be delivered and returned.
statements.policyBackground: Universal mail-in voting means every registered voter automatically receives a ballot by mail rather than having to request one. Supporters say it makes voting easier, while opponents raise concerns about ballot security and the chain of custody of mailed ballots.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: Universal mail-in ballots for all registered voters. A true independent, public riven redistricting process.

statements.text: California should draw its election district maps through elected officials rather than an independent process.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_raji_rab: Supports universal mail-in ballots for all registered voters and an independent redistricting process.

statements.raceInsight: The way district lines are drawn affects which candidates are competitive and how fairly voters are represented. California's voters have a direct stake in who draws these maps.
statements.policyBackground: Election district maps define the geographic boundaries used to elect representatives. An independent process uses a commission or other body not made up of elected officials to draw these boundaries. The statement concerns which body should be responsible for drawing district lines.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: Universal mail-in ballots for all registered voters. A true independent, public riven redistricting process.

statements.draft: California should draw its election district maps through an independent process instead of by elected officials.

statements.text: The United States should continue providing financial aid to Israel.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_don_j_grundmann: Grundmann states there should be no further U.S. funding for Israel.

statements.raceInsight: U.S. aid to Israel is one of the largest and most debated lines in American foreign spending, and Californians hold a wide range of views on it. The question also ties into broader concerns about the Middle East and the use of U.S. military assistance.
statements.policyBackground: The United States has provided Israel with military and economic assistance for decades, usually in multi-year agreements approved by Congress. Supporters see this aid as a security partnership, while critics question its cost and how it is used.

statements.topic: State rules on boycotts of Israel
statements.text: States should be allowed to require companies that do business with them to pledge not to boycott Israel.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_eric_swalwell: Co-sponsored the Israel Anti-Boycott Act, which would let states require contractors to pledge not to boycott Israel or Israeli-occupied territories.

statements.raceInsight: Californians are divided over whether state governments should limit how public contractors take part in political boycotts. The issue touches on free speech, state contracting, and U.S. relations with Israel.
statements.policyBackground: A boycott is a refusal to buy from, sell to, or work with a person, business, or country as a form of protest. Some states already require contractors to certify they are not boycotting Israel, and critics argue such rules may limit free expression.

ca_gov_primary_eric_swalwell.quote: In 2017, Swalwell co-sponsored the Israel Anti-Boycott Act, a House bill designed to allow U.S. states to enact laws requiring contractors to sign pledges promising not to boycott any goods from Israel and Israeli-occupied territories or their contracts would be terminated.

statements.text: Turkey's membership in NATO should be suspended.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_eric_swalwell: Condemned the 2019 Turkish offensive in Syria and called for possibly suspending Turkey's NATO membership.

statements.raceInsight: NATO is the central security alliance for the United States and its partners, and Turkey is one of its largest members. Voters care about how the alliance responds when a member's actions conflict with shared goals.
statements.policyBackground: NATO is a military alliance of North American and European countries that agree to defend one another. The alliance has no formal procedure for removing a member, so any suspension would be a major and contested step.

ca_gov_primary_eric_swalwell.quote: He condemned the 2019 Turkish offensive into northeastern Syria and called for possibly suspending Turkey 's membership in NATO.

statements.text: The United States should close the Russian embassy in Washington.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_eric_swalwell: Proposed closing the Russian embassy in the United States and expelling Russian students in response to the invasion of Ukraine.

statements.raceInsight: Russia's war in Ukraine has made U.S. responses to Moscow a major foreign policy question. Californians with ties to Ukraine, Russia, and Eastern Europe may weigh these choices differently.
statements.policyBackground: An embassy is the official diplomatic office of one country in another. Closing an embassy is one of the strongest diplomatic steps short of breaking relations, and governments use it to signal displeasure.

ca_gov_primary_eric_swalwell.quote: In 2022, Swalwell proposed measures such as closing the Russian embassy in the United States and expelling Russian students as part of a broader response to the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

statements.text: The United States should continue admitting Russian students on student visas.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_eric_swalwell: Proposed closing the Russian embassy in the United States and expelling Russian students in response to the invasion of Ukraine.

statements.raceInsight: Foreign students bring both academic and economic ties to California's universities. Policies on who may study in the United States raise questions about security, education, and international relations.
statements.policyBackground: A student visa is an official permission that allows a foreign national to enter a country to study. Russian students are people who are citizens of Russia enrolled or seeking enrollment in educational programs. The statement concerns admission for study, not other categories of entry.

ca_gov_primary_eric_swalwell.quote: In 2022, Swalwell proposed measures such as closing the Russian embassy in the United States and expelling Russian students as part of a broader response to the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

statements.draft: The United States should expel Russian students from the country.

statements.topic: Tariffs as a tool against China
statements.text: The United States should use tariffs as a main tool to pressure China over trade practices.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_eric_swalwell: Criticized Trump's trade war against China.

statements.raceInsight: Trade with China affects California's ports, farms, and technology sector, so tariff policy has direct effects on jobs and prices. Voters often weigh these economic effects against national security concerns.
statements.policyBackground: A tariff is a tax on imported goods, and governments sometimes use them to influence trade practices or other countries' behavior. Tariffs can raise costs for consumers and businesses, and economists debate how effective they are as pressure tools.

ca_gov_primary_eric_swalwell.quote: In 2019, Swalwell criticized Trump's trade war against China.

statements.text: California should require eligible young men in the state to register for the military draft.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz: Would ban draft registration in California and close all military bases.

statements.raceInsight: California has a large population of young adults who would be affected by any draft, and the state's relationship with the military is significant. Voters may have strong views on whether state government should have a role in military recruitment.
statements.policyBackground: Draft registration is enrollment with the Selective Service System, which maintains a list that could be used for military conscription. Under current federal law, most men aged 18 to 25 must register. The state-level question concerns whether California would require or support this registration.

ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz.quote: WE'LL BAN REGISTRATION FOR THE DRAFT IN CA +CLOSE ALL MILITARY BASES to stop crimes against humanity + war crimes.

statements.draft: California should prohibit draft registration within the state.

statements.text: All U.S. military bases in California should remain open.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz: Would ban draft registration in California and close all military bases.

statements.raceInsight: Military bases are major employers and economic drivers in several California regions, and they also shape national defense planning. Voters weigh jobs and local spending against security needs and base impacts.
statements.policyBackground: A military base is a installation used by the armed forces for training, operations, or housing personnel. Base closures are decisions to end a base's military use, which can be made through a federal process. Keeping a base open means continuing its current military operations.

ca_gov_primary_frederic_c_schultz.quote: WE'LL BAN REGISTRATION FOR THE DRAFT IN CA +CLOSE ALL MILITARY BASES to stop crimes against humanity + war crimes.

statements.draft: All U.S. military bases in California should be closed.

statements.text: The United States should maintain its economic embargo on Cuba.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_margaret_trowe: Calls for ending the U.S. economic blockade of Cuba and for U.S. hands off Cuba.

statements.raceInsight: California has a large Cuban-American community and a long history of trade and travel links across the Pacific and Caribbean. Voters in the state have strong and differing views on how Washington should treat the Cuban government.
statements.policyBackground: An economic embargo is a set of government restrictions on trade and financial transactions with a country. The U.S. embargo on Cuba dates to the early 1960s and has been modified over time. Maintaining it means keeping these restrictions in place.

ca_gov_primary_margaret_trowe.quote: "U.S. Hands off Cuba! End U.S. Economic Blockade of Cuba!"

statements.draft: The United States should end its economic embargo on Cuba.

statements.text: Water prices should reflect local supply and delivery costs in each water district.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_randeep_s_dhillon: Would protect California agriculture by ensuring fair, reliable, and affordable water, including consistent pricing across water districts.

statements.raceInsight: Water costs affect farm budgets, food prices, and households across California, and districts often charge different rates for similar supplies. Voters in farming regions and in cities both have a stake in how water is priced.
statements.policyBackground: Water districts are local public agencies that supply water to households and businesses in a defined area. Their prices can vary based on the costs of sourcing, treating, and delivering water in each region. The rewrite describes the position of those who favor district-level pricing.

ca_gov_primary_randeep_s_dhillon.quote: As Governor, I will protect California agriculture by ensuring fair, reliable, and affordable water, including consistent pricing across water districts so farmers can plan, invest, and produce.

statements.draft: Water prices should be the same across all water districts in California.

statements.text: The state should be able to require farmers to switch to crops that use less water.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_serge_fiankan: Serge Fiankan's water plan avoids forced crop switching and uncompensated pumping bans, treating farmers as partners.

statements.raceInsight: Drought and limited supplies force hard choices about which crops get grown and where water goes. How much the government should direct those choices affects farm income, rural jobs, and food supply.
statements.policyBackground: Crop switching means changing which crops are planted, often toward crops that need less water. A mandatory version would require farmers to change crops, while a voluntary version would rely on incentives or farmer choice.

ca_gov_primary_serge_fiankan.quote: The plan explicitly avoids forced crop switching and uncompensated pumping bans, and treats farmers as partners with paid recharge and cost-shared upgrades.

statements.text: California should keep its existing water rights system rather than overhauling it.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_raji_rab: Says California's water rights need resetting for its growing population and calls for water reforms.

statements.raceInsight: Water rights decide who may use the state's limited water supply, and population growth and climate change are putting pressure on that system. Changes to these rules could affect cities, farms, and the environment.
statements.policyBackground: Water rights are legal entitlements that determine who may use water from rivers, lakes, and aquifers and under what conditions. An overhaul would substantially change how these entitlements are allocated, recorded, or transferred. The statement concerns whether the current framework should stay in place.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: The water rights need resetting for our growing population. Water reforms are needed due to the water shortages to set a fair relief for all.

statements.draft: California should overhaul its water rights system.

statements.text: The state should focus water investment on large regional reservoirs and conveyance systems rather than small rural reservoirs.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri: He would fund smaller recycling reservoirs for rural communities to be more self-sustaining during droughts.

statements.raceInsight: Many rural communities depend on a single water source that can run low during droughts. Local storage and reuse projects are one way to reduce that risk, and they involve public spending decisions voters may weigh differently.
statements.policyBackground: Water recycling reservoirs store treated wastewater or recycled water for later use, such as irrigation or other non-drinking purposes. Large regional reservoirs and conveyance systems are major water storage and transport projects that serve many communities. This statement concerns which scale of water infrastructure the state should prioritize.

ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri.quote: Fund smaller recycling reservoirs for rural communities so they can be more self-sustaining during droughts when metropolitan areas are overburdened.

statements.draft: The state should fund small water recycling reservoirs for rural communities.

statements.text: The state should regularly audit its spending to find and cut waste.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_betty_t_yee: Yee says she uncovered $7.3 billion in misspending.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_joseph_cabrera: Cabrera plans to fund schools and clinics by auditing projects he calls ghost projects and redirecting interest savings, without raising taxes.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer: Steyer says he will conduct a full spending review and quickly build emergency housing so people can spend nights indoors with access to care.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_elaine_culotti: Would ensure full transparency in how tax dollars are spent and uncover fraud, which aligns with regular state audits to find and cut waste.

statements.raceInsight: State spending in California runs into the tens of billions of dollars each year, so voters often ask whether public money is being used well. How and how often the state checks its own spending affects how much room there is for other priorities.
statements.policyBackground: A state audit is a review of how public money was spent to check whether it was used as intended and whether it was used efficiently. Audits can be routine or targeted at specific programs or projects. Supporters say they reveal waste, while critics say they can be slow or costly and may not change outcomes.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: As Governor, I will conduct a full spending review, partner with local governments to identify and implement approaches that work across all levels of need, and quickly build emergency housing so people on the street can spend the night indoors with access to care.

ca_gov_primary_joseph_cabrera.quote: By auditing "ghost projects" and redirecting interest savings, we can fund our schools and clinics without raising your taxes.

ca_gov_primary_elaine_culotti.quote: Power Back to the People by restoring local control, ending unfunded mandates, uncovering fraud, and ensuring full transparency in how tax dollars are spent.

statements.topic: Balancing the budget without raising taxes
statements.text: The state should avoid raising taxes to balance its budget.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_joseph_cabrera: Cabrera plans to fund schools and clinics by auditing projects he calls ghost projects and redirecting interest savings, without raising taxes.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell: Supports managing the state budget wisely, monitoring spending carefully, and using every dollar effectively instead of creating new tax structures.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_raji_rab: Plans to lower taxes and provide tax relief for businesses and job creators.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer: Steyer says he will close corporate tax loopholes and raise $20 billion in new revenue each year for education, healthcare, childcare, and home care.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_elaine_culotti: Would reduce anti-growth tax burdens, which aligns with the state avoiding tax increases to balance its budget.

statements.raceInsight: California has some of the highest tax burdens in the country, and the state budget must be balanced every year. Whether the state covers its costs through taxes, spending changes, or other means is a central choice for voters.
statements.policyBackground: A state budget sets how much money is collected and how much is spent. Raising taxes or creating new tax structures increases revenue, while other approaches focus on cutting costs, reallocating funds, or finding savings. Supporters of avoiding tax increases argue they protect household budgets, while others argue that revenue increases are needed to fund services.

ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.quote: Instead of creating new and uncertain tax structures, we should focus on managing our budget wisely, monitoring spending carefully, and ensuring every dollar is used effectively.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I'll lower taxes to lower costs and lead California in civil rights, best healthcare, income, education, trade, infrastructure and space age advancement.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: Tom is going to close these corporate loopholes, and raise $20 billion of new revenue each year to fund things like education, healthcare, childcare, and home care, all without charging working people a penny.

ca_gov_primary_joseph_cabrera.quote: By auditing "ghost projects" and redirecting interest savings, we can fund our schools and clinics without raising your taxes.

ca_gov_primary_elaine_culotti.quote: Bring jobs and investment back by reducing anti-growth tax burdens and regulatory drag.

statements.topic: Limiting state debt to one generation
statements.text: The state should be able to borrow for long-lived infrastructure with repayment periods longer than one generation.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri: He would cap state spending so that only debt payable within one generation could be incurred.

statements.raceInsight: California carries large amounts of public debt, and the length of time required to repay it shapes what future governments can fund. Voters weigh whether legal limits on borrowing are needed to keep long-term obligations manageable.
statements.policyBackground: Public borrowing means government raising money by issuing bonds or other debt that must be repaid with interest. A generation is commonly understood as roughly 20 to 30 years. This statement concerns whether debt for long-lasting public assets may be repaid over a span longer than that.

ca_gov_primary_daniel_mercuri.quote: Implement a cap on state government spending that would only allow the incurring of a debt that could be paid off in one generation.

statements.draft: The state should limit its borrowing to debt that can be repaid within one generation.

statements.text: California should reduce regulations on small businesses.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_raji_rab: Plans to ease regulations and offer relief to small businesses.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_randeep_s_dhillon: Would reduce regulations and expand access to capital for small businesses.

statements.raceInsight: Small businesses employ a large share of California's workers, so the rules that apply to them affect jobs, prices, and local economies in every region. Voters often weigh how much oversight protects consumers and workers against how much it adds to the cost of starting and running a business.
statements.policyBackground: Business regulations are government rules covering things like licensing, permits, reporting, labor standards, and environmental compliance. Supporters of reducing them argue that fewer or simpler rules lower costs for small firms, while critics argue that some rules protect workers, consumers, and the environment.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I will offer relief to small businesses from burdensome regulations and boost small business conditions for expansion.

ca_gov_primary_randeep_s_dhillon.quote: I will stand with small businesses by reducing regulations and expanding access to capital so entrepreneurs can grow and hire.

statements.text: Social goals are best reached through capitalism rather than socialism.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_scott_p_shields: Shields states that social solutions are best achieved with capitalism and freedoms.
candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_ramsey_robinson: Says they are fighting for socialism, meaning a system where working people hold political and economic power to meet their needs.

statements.raceInsight: The choice between market-based and government-led economic systems shapes how California approaches housing, wages, taxes, and public services. Voters may want to know which economic model a candidate would prioritize for solving social problems.
statements.policyBackground: Capitalism generally refers to an economy where private individuals and companies own most businesses and markets set prices. Socialism generally refers to an economy where the community or the state owns or controls major economic resources, with the goal of meeting people's needs.

ca_gov_primary_scott_p_shields.quote: Social solutions are best achieved with capitalism and freedoms.

ca_gov_primary_ramsey_robinson.quote: I'm fighting for socialism—a system where we working people have the political and economic power to meet our needs.

statements.text: California should expand partnerships between government and private companies to fund public projects.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell: Supports strengthening public-private partnerships and encouraging civic investment to rebuild the state.

statements.raceInsight: California faces large needs for roads, water, transit, and other infrastructure, and voters differ on whether private money should play a bigger role in paying for them. How these projects are financed affects public costs, control, and long-term obligations.
statements.policyBackground: A public-private partnership is an arrangement in which a government agency and a private company share the work, funding, or risk of a public project. Supporters say it can bring in private capital and efficiency, while critics raise concerns about cost, accountability, and long-term public control.

ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.quote: By strengthening public–private partnerships and encouraging civic investment, we can rebuild our state without relying on policies that risk driving away innovation, jobs, and opportunity.

statements.text: California should launch its own state cryptocurrency.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_scott_p_shields: Shields states that California should launch a California crypto coin to fill the void left by Warren Buffett's retirement.

statements.raceInsight: Digital currencies and blockchain tools are growing parts of the financial system, and California is home to many companies working in this area. Voters may weigh the benefits of a state-issued digital asset against financial risk and the role of government in money.
statements.policyBackground: A cryptocurrency is a digital currency that uses cryptography to track ownership, usually without a central bank. A state-issued cryptocurrency would be a digital currency created and backed by a state government rather than by private developers.

ca_gov_primary_scott_p_shields.quote: With Your Retiring, It Will Be Hard To Fill That Void So We Have To Launch The California Crypto Coin And We Appreciate All You Have Done.

statements.text: California should end its film tax credit program.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer: Steyer says he will support the film tax credit system to protect California's film industry.

statements.raceInsight: Film and television production supports many jobs across California, and states compete for productions through tax incentives. Voters may weigh the jobs and economic activity these credits bring against their cost to the state budget.
statements.policyBackground: A film tax credit reduces the state tax owed by productions that film or produce in California, typically based on qualifying spending. Ending the program would stop offering these reductions in future. Tax credits lower the amount of tax a business or individual must pay.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: Tom will support our tax credit system to protect California’s film industry.

statements.draft: California should keep its film tax credit program.

statements.text: Congress should pass the Merger Filing Fee Modernization Act of 2022.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_eric_swalwell: Swalwell voted against the Merger Filing Fee Modernization Act of 2022.
