item.draft: California should require affordable homes to stay affordable for 30 to 55 years.

flags.name: Ask without leaning
flags.detail: dropped for loaded wording ('Regardless of their per-unit cost' is a framing no real advocate would use and makes disagreement sound obvious.)

item.text: State housing funds should prioritize supportive housing projects regardless of their per-unit cost.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_satish_rao: Argues that supportive housing at People's Park-level costs is too expensive and that cheaper housing options would be better elsewhere.

item.raceInsight: Construction costs for supportive housing have drawn attention because the price per unit can be very high. Voters weigh how much each unit costs against how many people can be housed.
item.policyBackground: Supportive housing combines affordable housing with on-site services such as health care or counseling for residents who need them. Per-unit cost is the total cost of a project divided by the number of housing units it creates. Whether cost should be a main factor in choosing which housing projects to fund is a matter of debate.

ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.quote: The same housing would be substantially cheaper and perhaps more beneficial for many in other areas.

item.draft: Lower-cost housing options should be preferred over high-cost supportive housing projects.

flags.name: Ask without leaning
flags.detail: dropped for loaded wording (Few if any real candidates or groups would put the position this way. It reads as a strawman of rejecting federal money.)

item.text: California should not seek federal funding to help residents with housing costs.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_raji_rab: Plans to seek federal funding and offer housing plans to ease down payment, mortgage, rent and utility costs.

item.raceInsight: Many Californians spend a large share of their income on housing and utilities, and federal dollars can significantly affect what state programs can offer. Voters may consider how much to rely on federal support versus state resources.
item.policyBackground: Federal funding is money appropriated by the U.S. government that states can apply for or receive for specific programs. Housing costs refer to what residents pay for rent, mortgages, and related expenses. Whether a state seeks such funds is a choice made by state officials and the legislature.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I will seek federal funding to ease burdensome complexities and offer real housing plans to ease down payment, mortgage, rent and utilities.

item.draft: California should seek federal funding to help residents pay for housing costs.

flags.name: Ask without leaning
flags.detail: dropped for loaded wording (A bare 'cut funding' framing with no stated reason resembles the 'X should be weakened' pattern and few would frame it that way.)

item.text: The state should cut funding for public colleges and universities.

candidatePositions.ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa: Says he secured over $1.5 billion for UC, CSU, and community colleges.

item.raceInsight: State funding helps keep tuition lower and supports the programs students use. Voters differ on how much of the state budget should go to higher education.
item.policyBackground: State funding refers to money the state government appropriates to public colleges and universities, usually through the annual budget. Public colleges and universities are higher education institutions owned and operated by state or local governments. Budget decisions about these institutions are made by the governor and the state legislature.

ca_gov_primary_antonio_villaraigosa.quote: Secured over $1.5 billion for UC, CSU, and community colleges

item.draft: The state should increase funding for public colleges and universities.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "California should allow new oil wells to be drilled closer than 3,200 " had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: California should allow new oil wells to be drilled closer than 3,200 feet from homes and schools.
item.raceInsight: Where oil wells can be placed relative to homes and other sites affects air quality and public health in nearby communities. Voters have different views on how strictly drilling should be limited near people.
item.policyBackground: The 3,200-foot setback law requires new oil wells to be located at least that distance from homes, schools, and similar sites. A setback is a required minimum distance between a development and a protected location. The rewrite describes the position of those who would reduce or remove that distance requirement.
item.draft: California should fully enforce its 3,200-foot setback law for new oil wells.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "California should not use automatic payments to consumers when fuel pr" had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: California should not use automatic payments to consumers when fuel prices rise.
item.raceInsight: Sudden fuel price spikes can strain household budgets, and voters differ on whether relief should happen automatically or be decided case by case. The design of any trigger affects when payments go out.
item.policyBackground: An automatic relief payment is a direct payment to consumers that is triggered when fuel prices reach a set level, without a new legislative vote. A fuel price trigger is a predetermined price threshold that activates such a policy. The rewrite describes the position of those who prefer that relief be decided case by case instead.
item.draft: California should automatically pay relief to consumers when fuel prices reach a set trigger.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "The state should not earmark funding for school staff such as reading " had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: The state should not earmark funding for school staff such as reading specialists and counselors and should leave staffing decisions to local school districts.
item.raceInsight: Students' reading skills and mental health affect their progress in school. Voters differ on how much of school budgets should go to specialized staff compared with other needs.
item.policyBackground: Reading specialists support students with literacy instruction, and school counselors provide academic, college, and personal guidance. An earmark is state funding restricted to a specific purpose, while local school districts are the agencies that run schools in their areas.
item.draft: The state should fund more school staff such as reading specialists and counselors.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "The state should prioritize need-based grants over college savings acc" had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.topic: College savings accounts for vulnerable students
item.text: The state should prioritize need-based grants over college savings accounts for students.
item.raceInsight: Saving for college can be difficult for families with limited income, and savings accounts can help students plan for higher education. Voters differ on the role of state-supported savings programs.
item.policyBackground: College savings accounts are tax-advantaged accounts that families use to save for education costs. Need-based grants are funds awarded to students based on financial circumstances and generally do not require repayment. The statement concerns whether state education dollars should go mainly to grants rather than to savings accounts.
item.draft: The state should expand college savings accounts for vulnerable students.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "The state should not mandate smaller class sizes in elementary schools" had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: The state should not mandate smaller class sizes in elementary schools, leaving those decisions to local districts.
item.raceInsight: The number of students per teacher affects how much individual attention children receive. Voters often disagree on whether limiting class size is worth its cost compared with other uses of school money.
item.policyBackground: Class size refers to the number of students assigned to one teacher in a classroom. Elementary schools serve young students, typically in kindergarten through fifth or sixth grade. Local school districts are public agencies that govern schools within a specific geographic area.
item.draft: The state should reduce class sizes in elementary schools.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "Public universities should consider applicants' background and life ex" had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: Public universities should consider applicants' background and life experience alongside test scores in admissions.
item.raceInsight: Admissions rules at public universities shape who gets into the state's most sought-after colleges. Voters differ on how admissions should weigh academic achievement against other factors.
item.policyBackground: Merit-based admissions generally rank applicants primarily by academic measures such as grades and test scores. Holistic review considers a wider range of factors, including personal background and experiences. The rewrite describes the position of those who favor broader admissions criteria over a primarily merit-based model.
item.draft: California should return public universities to a merit-based admissions model.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "Israel has a right to exist and to defend itself." had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.topic: Israel's right to exist and defend itself
item.text: Israel has a right to exist and to defend itself.
item.raceInsight: Views on Israel's security and right to self-defense shape how Californians, who include large Jewish, Arab, and Muslim communities, judge U.S. policy in the region. Many voters want to know where candidates stand on this core question.
item.policyBackground: This statement concerns whether Israel, as a state, is entitled to exist and to use force to protect its population. It is a central point of disagreement in debates about the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and U.S. policy.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "The state should be allowed to borrow money to cover its regular opera" had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: The state should be allowed to borrow money to cover its regular operating bills when revenues fall short.
item.raceInsight: How California finances its obligations affects future budgets and the taxes or cuts that may follow. Voters care about whether today's bills are paid with today's revenue or with money that must be repaid later.
item.policyBackground: Regular operating bills are the routine costs of running state government, such as salaries and services. Borrowing means issuing debt, typically short-term, to cover costs before or when revenue is insufficient. The rewrite describes the position of those who support using borrowing for these ordinary expenses.
item.draft: The state should not borrow money to pay its regular bills.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "Government income support should be limited to people who pass a needs" had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: Government income support should be limited to people who pass a needs-based test rather than paid to everyone.
item.raceInsight: Proposals for guaranteed income have drawn attention as a response to rising living costs and changes in work. Voters may weigh the potential reduction in poverty against the cost and effect on work incentives.
item.policyBackground: A guaranteed basic income is a regular cash payment made to individuals without a work requirement. A needs-based test is an eligibility process that considers a person's income or resources. Programs using such tests direct benefits to those below set thresholds.
item.draft: The government should guarantee every adult and child a regular basic income.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "Federal law should not add sexual orientation and gender identity to a" had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: Federal law should not add sexual orientation and gender identity to anti-discrimination protections in housing and employment.
item.raceInsight: Housing and job discrimination rules affect everyday life for LGBTQ+ Californians, and California has its own state-level protections that the governor helps administer. Voters may consider how state and federal protections compare and which level of government should set them.
item.policyBackground: Federal anti-discrimination law bars certain treatment in housing and employment based on listed traits such as race, sex, and religion. Sexual orientation refers to a person's romantic or sexual attraction, and gender identity refers to a person's internal sense of their own gender. The statement concerns whether these two traits would be added to that list of protected categories.
item.draft: Federal law should prohibit discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity in housing and employment.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "Workers' right to form unions should be governed by federal law rather" had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: Workers' right to form unions should be governed by federal law rather than new California statutes.
item.raceInsight: Whether workers can organize affects wages, workplace safety, and job conditions across many California industries. The question also shapes how employers and workers bargain over the terms of everyday jobs.
item.policyBackground: A union is an organization of workers that bargains collectively with employers over pay and working conditions. Federal law and state law can both set rules for union organizing, and a statute is a law passed by a legislature.
item.draft: California should create and enforce workers' right to form unions.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "The state should leave paid leave for parents of a newborn or newly ad" had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: The state should leave paid leave for parents of a newborn or newly adopted child to employers and private arrangements rather than mandate state-funded paid leave.
item.raceInsight: Paid time off after a birth or adoption affects family finances, child health, and whether parents can stay in the workforce. Voters weigh how such benefits should be funded and who should receive them.
item.policyBackground: Paid leave for new parents is time off from work after a birth or adoption that is paid through wages or benefits. A state-funded program would be administered and financed by the government rather than by individual employers. This statement concerns whether that benefit should be provided by the state or left to the private sector.
item.draft: The state should offer 24 weeks of paid leave to parents of a newborn or newly adopted child.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "Candidates for office should be allowed to accept campaign contributio" had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: Candidates for office should be allowed to accept campaign contributions from corporations and corporate political action committees.
item.raceInsight: Voters in California see campaign money as a central question for state leaders, since large donations can shape which issues get attention in Sacramento. Rules on where campaign money comes from affect how much trust voters place in elected officials.
item.policyBackground: A corporate political action committee, or PAC, is a fundraising committee sponsored by a company that collects money from its employees or shareholders to support candidates. Campaign contributions are donations given directly to candidates for their election efforts.
item.draft: Candidates for office should refuse campaign contributions from corporations and corporate political action committees.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "California should keep the state Supreme Court at seven justices." had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: California should keep the state Supreme Court at seven justices.
item.raceInsight: The number of justices on the state's highest court affects how cases are heard and how the court's workload is shared. Changes to the court's size are a significant structural question that voters may weigh when considering the state's judicial system.
item.policyBackground: The California Supreme Court is the highest court in the state's judicial system. The number of justices is set in the state constitution, and seven is the current number.
item.draft: California should expand the state Supreme Court to 13 justices.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "California should keep its animal cruelty laws at their current scope " had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: California should keep its animal cruelty laws at their current scope rather than expanding them.
item.raceInsight: Animal cruelty laws affect pets, farm animals, and wildlife across the state, and voters often weigh how strictly these laws should be applied and enforced. The issue also touches local shelters, law enforcement budgets, and the cost of animal care programs.
item.policyBackground: Animal cruelty laws are state statutes that prohibit harming, neglecting, or abusing animals, and they define which acts and animals are covered. Expanding these laws would broaden the conduct or types of animals they cover. The statement concerns whether California's existing laws should remain as they are.
item.draft: California should expand legal protections for animals against cruelty.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "California should increase state funding for social services relative " had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.topic: State funding priority for public safety services
item.text: California should increase state funding for social services relative to police funding.
item.raceInsight: Police, fire, and emergency medical services are funded through state and local budgets, so decisions about priorities affect response times and public safety statewide.
item.policyBackground: Social services are government programs that provide assistance such as food, income support, or counseling to residents in need. State funding refers to money appropriated from the state budget to local governments or programs. Budget priorities determine how much each program area receives relative to others.
item.draft: State funding should prioritize police, fire, and emergency medical services.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "California should maintain current state funding for county jails." had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.topic: Mental health treatment instead of jail
item.text: California should maintain current state funding for county jails.
item.raceInsight: Many people in California jails have mental illness, and county jails are often the main place where they are held. Voters often weigh public safety, county budgets, and access to treatment when considering this issue.
item.policyBackground: County jails are local facilities that hold people awaiting trial and those sentenced to short terms. State funding for jails is money the state budget provides to counties to operate or support these facilities. Community mental health treatment refers to services that address mental health needs in community settings rather than in jails.
item.draft: California should move funding from jails to community mental health treatment.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "Government should avoid lockdowns during pandemics." had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: Government should avoid lockdowns during pandemics.
item.raceInsight: Pandemic-era rules such as stay-at-home orders, masking, and business closures affected schools, jobs, and daily life across California. Voters differ on how much authority government should have in future health emergencies.
item.policyBackground: A lockdown is a government order that restricts movement or closes businesses and public spaces to slow the spread of a contagious disease. Pandemics are widespread outbreaks of infectious disease. Whether lockdowns are an appropriate tool is a question on which people hold differing views.
item.draft: Government should avoid lockdowns and required public health mandates during pandemics.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "California should provide broad tax relief that applies to all taxpaye" had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: California should provide broad tax relief that applies to all taxpayers.
item.raceInsight: Many older Californians and people on fixed incomes have limited ability to absorb rising costs. Voters consider how targeted tax relief compares with broader tax cuts in helping these households.
item.policyBackground: Tax relief refers to reductions in the taxes that residents or businesses owe, such as through lower rates or credits. Broad, across-the-board relief applies to all taxpayers in the same way. Supporters and critics debate which approach best serves the state's budget and residents.
item.draft: California should provide targeted tax relief for seniors and people on fixed incomes.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "California should focus its affordable housing assistance on rental un" had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: California should focus its affordable housing assistance on rental units.
item.raceInsight: Many renters in California cannot save enough for a down payment, so programs that let renters build toward ownership affect how many households can become homeowners. Voters may consider whether a small trial program is an effective way to expand homeownership.
item.policyBackground: Affordable housing assistance refers to public funding, subsidies, or programs that help make housing more affordable. Rental units are homes that residents lease from an owner rather than own. Decisions about which housing types receive assistance are a budget and policy question.
item.draft: California should create a pilot program that helps qualified affordable housing residents move toward owning their homes.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "The state should prioritize climate and clean-energy goals in grid pla" had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: The state should prioritize climate and clean-energy goals in grid planning.
item.raceInsight: Power outages affect health, businesses, and emergency services, and wildfire and drought conditions are testing the grid. Voters care how the state balances reliability with other energy goals.
item.policyBackground: Grid planning is the process of deciding how the state's electricity system is built, expanded, and operated over time. Climate goals are targets for reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and clean-energy goals are targets for increasing power from sources such as solar, wind, and storage.
item.draft: The state should prioritize a reliable electric grid that avoids blackouts.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "Private charities, rather than government programs, should be the main" had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.topic: Veteran homelessness through housing and jobs
item.text: Private charities, rather than government programs, should be the main providers of help for homeless veterans.
item.raceInsight: California has one of the largest populations of homeless veterans in the country, making veteran homelessness a visible concern. Voters will consider which federal, state, and local tools should be used to address it.
item.policyBackground: Private charities are nonprofit organizations funded mainly by donations that provide services such as shelter, food, and job training. Government programs are services funded and run by public agencies at the federal, state, or local level. Homeless veterans are military veterans who lack stable, permanent housing.
item.draft: Government should address veteran homelessness through housing and employment programs.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "Funding from declining K-12 enrollment should be redirected to other s" had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: Funding from declining K-12 enrollment should be redirected to other state priorities.
item.raceInsight: Fewer students in California's public schools change how much funding districts receive and how many staff they need. Voters differ on how savings from shrinking enrollment should be used.
item.policyBackground: K-12 enrollment refers to the number of students attending public schools from kindergarten through twelfth grade. Declining enrollment means the number of students is falling, which can change how much funding a school system receives. Redirecting funding means moving money from one budget area to another, as decided by state lawmakers.
item.draft: Funding saved from declining K-12 enrollment should be used to raise pay for remaining teachers.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "Voting systems should not provide voters with take-home paper receipts" had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: Voting systems should not provide voters with take-home paper receipts of their ballot choices.
item.raceInsight: Voters want assurance that their ballot was counted as they intended, especially as California's large number of voters use different voting methods. A receipt that can be checked is one way to give that assurance.
item.policyBackground: A take-home paper receipt is a printed record of a voter's selections that the voter keeps after casting a ballot. Voting systems are the equipment, software, and procedures used to record and count votes. This statement concerns only receipts a voter takes home, not paper ballots that are kept by election officials.
item.draft: Voters should receive a receipt they can use to check that their vote was recorded correctly.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "California should prioritize ground crews over aerial firefighting." had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.topic: Aerial firefighting and early wildfire detection
item.text: California should prioritize ground crews over aerial firefighting.
item.raceInsight: Wildfires have destroyed homes and forced evacuations across California in recent years. How quickly fires are spotted and how they are attacked from the air can change how much damage they cause.
item.policyBackground: Ground crews are firefighters who battle wildfires on foot or with hand and vehicle equipment. Aerial firefighting uses aircraft, such as planes and helicopters, to drop water or fire retardant on wildfires. Prioritizing one means directing more budget and resources toward it.
item.draft: California should expand aerial firefighting and early wildfire detection systems.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "Government should involve regulated industries directly in drafting po" had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: Government should involve regulated industries directly in drafting policy rules.
item.raceInsight: Voters often worry that well-connected groups have outsized influence over decisions that affect everyday residents. How officials disclose contacts and limit special access shapes public confidence in government.
item.policyBackground: Regulated industries are businesses that government agencies oversee through rules and licensing, such as energy or banking firms. Drafting policy rules means writing the specific requirements that will later be enforced. Direct involvement could include formal consultation, advisory committees, or industry-submitted proposals.
item.draft: Government should restrict the influence of insiders over policy decisions.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "California should rely more on private developers than on public fundi" had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: California should rely more on private developers than on public funding to build affordable housing.
item.raceInsight: Housing and transportation costs and access shape whether people with disabilities can live independently and reach jobs, medical care, and community life. Voters across the state face rising housing costs and transit decisions that affect these outcomes.
item.policyBackground: Private developers are companies that build and finance housing for sale or rent. Public funding means money from government budgets, such as state or local housing programs. Affordable housing refers to homes whose rent or price is within reach of lower- and middle-income households.
item.draft: California should build more affordable housing and public transit that is accessible to people with disabilities.

flags.name: Don't fill the silence
flags.detail: dropped (after check): "California should guarantee a minimum income for older residents." had 0 scored candidate(s)

item.text: California should guarantee a minimum income for older residents.
item.raceInsight: Many Californians face uncertainty about whether savings, pensions, and Social Security will cover their later years, given the state's high housing and healthcare costs. Voters may weigh how much responsibility the state should take for retirement security compared with individuals and employers.
item.policyBackground: A guaranteed minimum income is a set amount of money that the government ensures each eligible person receives. Older residents are people who have reached retirement age. The policy would set a floor on income for this group, regardless of prior earnings.
item.draft: California should guarantee older residents a dignified retirement.

ca_gov_primary_akinyemi_agbede.stance: Supports expanding access to affordable housing while enhancing support services for homeless individuals.
ca_gov_primary_akinyemi_agbede.quote: Expanding access to affordable housing while enhancing support services for homeless individuals, ensuring stable living conditions and long-term solutions.

ca_gov_primary_akinyemi_agbede.stance: Supports creating jobs, supporting businesses, and implementing tax reforms to reduce the financial burden on families.
ca_gov_primary_akinyemi_agbede.quote: Creating job opportunities, supporting businesses, and implementing tax reforms to reduce the financial burden on families and foster economic prosperity.

ca_gov_primary_akinyemi_agbede.stance: Supports strengthening community policing and investing in crime prevention programs.
ca_gov_primary_akinyemi_agbede.quote: Strengthening community policing efforts and investing in crime prevention programs to enhance security, build trust, and create safer neighborhoods.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.stance: He states that health care is a human right and that he will deliver affordable care without debt or delays, strengthen Medi-Cal, and build toward Medicare for All.
ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: I know that health care is a human right. As California’s Health Care Governor I will deliver affordable care without debt or delays, strengthen Medi-Cal, close racial and economic gaps, and build toward Medicare for All.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.stance: As governor, he will ensure California continues to lead in protecting access to abortion.
ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: As Governor, I will ensure that California continues to lead when it comes to protecting access to abortion, to the ballot, and to live and love without restraint.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.stance: He says he voted against the Defense of Marriage Act in 1996.
ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: In 1996, I was among a small group of members of Congress to vote against the Defense of Marriage Act.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.stance: He will direct state agencies to protect access to essential health services from federal restrictions, including healthcare for immigrant communities.
ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: I will also direct state agencies to protect access to essential, medically appropriate health services from federal restrictions, including reproductive care and healthcare for immigrant communities, and ensure uninterrupted, equitable access to contraception, abortion, and maternal health support.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.stance: As governor, he will stand up to price gouging and unjustified rate hikes and use state power to lower prices where the market has failed.
ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: As Governor, I will take on the cost of living head-on by standing up to price gouging and unjustified rate hikes, expanding help with childcare and essential costs, and using the power of the state to lower prices where the market has failed.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.stance: He will negotiate maximum reimbursement rates for drugs bought through state programs and prioritize lower-cost biosimilars and therapeutic alternatives where clinically appropriate.
ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: I will negotiate maximum reimbursement rates for drugs purchased through state employee health plans, Medi-Cal, and all state-administered programs, and direct agencies to prioritize lower-cost biosimilars and therapeutic alternatives wherever clinically appropriate.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.stance: On day one, he will issue an executive order to maintain coverage continuity for Californians affected by federal cuts or Medi-Cal rollbacks.
ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: On Day One, I will issue an executive order directing state agencies to maintain coverage continuity for every Californian affected by federal cuts or Medi-Cal rollbacks.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.stance: He will fully implement Proposition 35 to dedicate MCO tax revenue to Medi-Cal.
ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: And I will fight to fully implement Proposition 35, which California voters passed in November 2024 to dedicate MCO tax revenue exclusively to Medi-Cal, ensuring those funds go to stronger provider payments and expanded access to care, not federal clawbacks.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.stance: He will create a dedicated healthcare fraud task force with authority to hold funds, investigate, file charges, and pursue cases to verdict.
ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: I will create a dedicated healthcare fraud task force with the authority to hold funds, investigate bad actors, file charges, and see cases through to verdict.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.stance: He will pursue a fee on large employers who do not offer health coverage to low-wage workers who qualify for Medi-Cal.
ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: I will pursue a fee on large employers who do not offer health coverage to their low-wage workers who qualify for Medi-Cal, so that corporations who shift their healthcare costs onto taxpayers pay their fair share.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.stance: He will require state-regulated payors to reimburse telehealth visits to the fullest extent permitted by law and expand specialty telehealth access.
ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: As Governor, I will issue an executive order requiring all state-regulated payors to reimburse telehealth visits to the fullest extent permitted under law, prioritizing telehealth delivered by California-licensed health care professionals through local and regional providers to provide urgent care for conditions that do not require an in-person visit, and leverage California’s volunteer physician registry to open specialty telehealth access to communities that have never had it.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.stance: He will expand access to safe, effective vaccines and restore trust in science as governor.
ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: As Governor, I will also strengthen public health infrastructure by restoring trust in science and expanding access to safe, effective vaccines, as I recognize immunization as one of the most powerful tools to prevent disease and protect public health.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.stance: On his first day as governor, he will declare California's housing shortage a state of emergency and make housing production the paramount priority.
ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: On my first day as Governor, I will issue an executive order declaring California’s housing shortage a state of emergency and directing every state agency to treat housing production and affordability as the paramount priority.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.stance: He will direct HCD to identify cities failing their housing element commitments and begin enforcement, including financial penalties where appropriate.
ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: I will direct the California Department of Housing and Community Development to immediately identify cities reneging on their housing element commitments and commence enforcement action, including financial penalties where appropriate.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.stance: He will expand California's down payment assistance program, increase its funding, and broaden eligibility.
ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: I will expand California’s down payment assistance program, increase its funding, and broaden eligibility so more first-time buyers can access it faster.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.stance: He will fully enforce the Tenant Protection Act and support local rent control within the statewide framework.
ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: I will enforce those protections fully and stand behind communities that have chosen to protect renters through local rent control, within the statewide framework that keeps housing construction moving forward.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.stance: He will establish a dedicated, stable funding stream for homelessness prevention tied to measurable reduction targets.
ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: As Governor, I would establish a dedicated, stable targeted homelessness prevention funding stream within the state’s homelessness response, one that communities can plan around year over year, tied to measurable reduction targets and local investment.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.stance: He says bill affordability will be central to his energy policy, especially for low- and middle-income families.
ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: Bill affordability will be at the center of my energy policy, especially for low- and middle-income families.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.stance: He will require data centers in California to add value to the energy infrastructure, use clean energy, cover their own energy costs, and meet environmental disclosure requirements.
ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: I will pursue an economic-forward standard: data centers that operate in California add value to our current energy infrastructure, are powered with clean energy, cover the costs of their own energy needs, and meet environmental performance disclosure requirements.

ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.stance: He will invest in wildfire prevention, flood control, and seismic retrofits, prioritizing the communities most at risk.
ca_gov_primary_xavier_becerra.quote: I will fight for major investments in wildfire prevention, flood control, and seismic retrofits, prioritizing the communities most at risk.

ca_gov_primary_derek_grasty.stance: Would keep ICE off California's streets.
ca_gov_primary_derek_grasty.quote: Together, we will keep kidnappers (ICE) off our streets, make housing affordable for working families, first responders, teachers, firefighters, and nurses.

ca_gov_primary_derek_grasty.stance: Supports affordable housing as part of a good quality of life for Californians.
ca_gov_primary_derek_grasty.quote: I believe that everyone should have a good quality of life. That means affordable housing, a safe community and a quality education.

ca_gov_primary_derek_grasty.stance: Would support education with pre-school, reading specialists, and mental health counselors.
ca_gov_primary_derek_grasty.quote: Education will be supported with pre-school, reading specialists, and mental health counselors to help our students thrive.

ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.stance: Opposes a wealth tax, saying it is not the way to address California's challenges.
ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.quote: California is facing real challenges, and we need real solutions — but a wealth tax is not the way to go.

ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.stance: Supports managing the state budget wisely, monitoring spending carefully, and using every dollar effectively instead of creating new tax structures.
ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.quote: Instead of creating new and uncertain tax structures, we should focus on managing our budget wisely, monitoring spending carefully, and ensuring every dollar is used effectively.

ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.stance: Supports strengthening public-private partnerships and encouraging civic investment to rebuild the state.
ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.quote: By strengthening public–private partnerships and encouraging civic investment, we can rebuild our state without relying on policies that risk driving away innovation, jobs, and opportunity.

ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.stance: Aims to lower grocery bills and protect families from unfair pricing.
ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.quote: Goal: Lower grocery bills and protect families from unfair pricing.

ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.stance: Proposes a mandatory pass-through of wholesale cost drops to consumers.
ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.quote: Mandatory pass‑through of wholesale cost drops

ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.stance: Aims to stabilize monthly utility bills and eliminate hidden fees.
ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.quote: Goal: Stabilize monthly bills and eliminate hidden fees.

ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.stance: Aims to reduce commuting costs and protect drivers.
ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.quote: Goal: Reduce commuting costs and protect drivers.

ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.stance: Aims to stabilize rents, expand housing supply, and lower monthly housing costs.
ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.quote: Goal: Stabilize rents, expand supply, and lower monthly costs.

ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.stance: Plans to convert vacant commercial buildings as part of the housing plan.
Aims to end insurance deserts and stop runaway insurance premiums.
ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.quote: Goal: End insurance deserts and stop runaway premiums.

ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.stance: Aims to make the system work for consumers rather than corporations.
ca_gov_primary_gary_howard_kidgell.quote: Goal: Make the system work for consumers, not corporations.

ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.stance: Says he will not ask Californians to pay more in taxes without results.
ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.quote: Matt won’t ask Californians to pay more in taxes without results.

ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.stance: Plans to drive down the cost of living, build more affordable housing, make cities safe, and ensure all kids have an opportunity to succeed.
ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.quote: He will work to drive down the cost of living, build more affordable housing, make our cities safe, and ensure all kids have an opportunity to succeed.

ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.stance: Advocated expanding law enforcement technologies, including license plate readers and speed cameras.
ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.quote: He advocated expanding the use of law enforcement technologies, including license plate readers and speed cameras.

ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.stance: Publicly supported stronger enforcement against drug trafficking in 2023 and 2024, while also promoting expanded treatment options.
ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.quote: In 2023 and 2024, Mahan publicly supported stronger enforcement against drug trafficking while also promoting expanded treatment options.

ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.stance: Endorsed California Proposition 36 in 2024, which increased sentences for certain theft and drug related crimes.
ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.quote: In 2024, in contrast to other state Democratic leaders, he endorsed California Proposition 36, which increased sentences for certain theft and drug related crimes.

ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.stance: Plans to get people off the streets, into treatment, and into housing.
ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.quote: He’s getting people off the streets, into treatment, and into housing.

ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.stance: In 2022 decreased funds for affordable housing to prioritize shelter construction, quick-build communities, and temporary housing.
ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.quote: In 2022, Mahan decreased the funds made available to affordable housing to prioritize shelter construction, quick-build communities, and temporary housing.

ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.stance: Pledged to end automatic raises for politicians and city department heads unless progress is shown.
ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.quote: He pledged to end automatic raises for politicians and city department heads unless progress is shown.

ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.stance: Opposed the August 2023 San Jose municipal union deal, arguing its increased costs would lead to a budget deficit and service cuts.
ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.quote: Mahan opposed an August 2023 deal with San Jose's municipal unions that raised employee wages and increased paid parental leave, arguing that the increased cost would lead to a budget deficit and force the city to cut services.

ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.stance: Said he would reluctantly support Proposition 50 despite concerns about partisan redistricting, while criticizing Newsom's combative approach.
ca_gov_primary_matt_mahan.quote: In 2025, as California’s Proposition 50 (a measure authorizing temporary legislatively drawn congressional maps) headed to the ballot, Mahan criticized Governor Gavin Newsom ’s combative approach to state/national politics and said he would reluctantly support the measure despite concerns about partisan redistricting.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.stance: Porter would eliminate state income tax for Californians earning less than $100,000.
ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: As Governor, I will work to eliminate state income tax for Californians making under $100,000. This will make a tangible difference in the lives of millions of people.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.stance: Porter would launch a progressive corporate tax that raises rates on the most profitable businesses.
ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: As Governor, I will launch a Progressive Corporate Tax. This is more than a one time windfall: this is a thoughtful and permanent structural shift that will incentivize businesses to invest their revenues in paying workers and expanding operations.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.stance: Porter plans to speed up housing construction by nearly two years and enforce housing laws to ensure prompt certificates of occupancy.
ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: I have a plan to speed up building by nearly two years, putting California on par with its peer states that also have worker and environmental protections. This will bring down the costs of apartment housing by 20%.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.stance: Porter's homelessness plan focuses on homeless prevention through emergency rental assistance and rapid re-housing, plus interim housing.
ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: My homelessness plan focuses on two strategies that California has not adopted: homeless prevention through emergency rental assistance and rapid re-housing, and interim housing that can keep people from being unsheltered, which is itself a risk factor for mental health and substance use problems.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.stance: Porter would deliver free child care for all, simplify the system into a one-stop shop, and raise provider wages.
ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: I will create a one-stop-shop that simplifies everything – a single, online form for providers to receive payment and for families to easily find the care that meets their needs.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.stance: Porter would make college tuition-free for all Californians by pairing community college with two free years at UC and CSU.
ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: As Governor, I will fulfill the forgotten promise of our state: tuition-free college for all Californians. By pairing two years of free community college, which already exists through the California College Promise, with two free years at our UC and CSU campuses, we will create a pathway for a four-year degree tuition-free.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.stance: Porter says she will work with federal partners to Abolish ICE.
ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: That’s why I will work with our federal partners to Abolish ICE.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.stance: Porter would fight Medi-Cal cuts and work to fortify California's health care system at the state level.
ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: As your Governor, I will fight these cuts with every fiber of my being and work to fortify our health care system at the state level so we can protect, expand and improve health care for all of our residents, while making sure our health care workforce has the support they need to care for Californians.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.stance: Porter supports single payer health care, known in California as CalCare, and would deliver it as governor.
ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: Single payer – known in California as CalCare – will deliver the highest quality AND most cost-effective care to the MOST people. Every policymaker should want that.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.stance: Porter says California must remain a state that protects and defends abortion rights, and she will do so as governor.
ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: California must remain a state that protects and defends abortion rights and when I’m Governor we will.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.stance: Porter says she has never taken money from corporations or corporate PACs and will not be influenced by special interests.
ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: I am the only person in this race who has never taken a dime from corporations or corporate PACs. Fighting corporate power is at the core of who I am and what I would bring as Governor.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.stance: Porter aims to accelerate clean energy by investing in renewables and expanding the grid, with a goal of 100% clean energy output.
ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: I will work to accelerate our transition to clean energy by investing in renewable resources like wind, solar, and geothermal, and expanding the grid to support these technologies.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.stance: Porter supports policies that create and enforce workers' right to unionize and aims to drive down costs for families.
ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: Every worker deserves a union. We must create – and enforce – policies that deliver that opportunity.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.stance: Porter pledges to keep fighting for LGBTQ+ rights to healthcare, housing, employment, and freedom to live as they choose.
ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: As Governor, I will never stop fighting for the LGBTQ+ community and their rights to healthcare, housing, employment, and the freedom to live however they choose.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.stance: Porter commits to holding officials and companies accountable to Californians with disabilities and to building more accessible, affordable housing and transit.
ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: As Governor, I am committed to holding public officials and private companies accountable to their responsibility to defend Californians with disabilities.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.stance: Porter has been a vocal supporter of Medicare for All.
ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: Since I entered politics a decade ago, I have never wavered in my support for Medicare for All.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.stance: Porter believes the government should have the power to negotiate drug prices.
ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: Porter stated that "there is simply no set of facts that supports that allowing the government to negotiate drug prices would reduce innovation" and that the government should have the power to negotiate drug prices and it would help create a more competitive market.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.stance: Porter supports H.R.1, which would undo the Supreme Court's Citizens United decision.
ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: She supported H.R.1 through the House of Representatives, which would undo the Supreme Court's Citizens United decision.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.stance: Porter supports more-stringent ethics codes for Supreme Court justices and legislation to expand the court to 13 justices.
ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: Porter has supported instituting more-stringent codes of conduct for the Supreme Court justices. In 2023, Demand Justice, an organization devoted to court reform and expansion, organized a statewide bus tour where Porter attended and put her support behind legislation that would expand the court to 13 justices.

ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.stance: Porter voted for H.R. 5, the Equality Act, which passed the House but failed in the Senate.
ca_gov_primary_katie_porter.quote: In 2019 and 2021, she voted in favor of H.R. 5, which passed in the House, but failed in the Senate.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Supports immigration amnesty for undocumented people who pay a fee, as a signature issue.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I support immigration Amnesty as my signature issue as it has become a humanitarian issue, an integrity issue and an issue of human dignity. It's time to face reality and embrace those already here, living with us and helping us for years in meeting our low budget and affordability crisis in so many areas of our daily lives.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Plans to expedite manufacturing of medications in California to reduce costs and dependence on imports.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I will expedite medication to be manufactured here in California to reduce costs, create thousands of high paying jobs, improve the economy, and ensure that we are not dependent on other countries.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Supports Medicare for All and full, free healthcare for every American.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I believe that healthcare rights are human rights, and every American deserves full and free healthcare with Medicare for All.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Supports women's right to reproductive health care access and privacy, including legal protection for out-of-state abortion patients and shielding their medical records.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I support women's right for reproductive health care access and privacy, legally protecting women who travel from other states to access abortion services here in California, including shielding their medical records.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Plans to double the existing $200 million for reproductive health care and birth control access.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I will double the existing $200 million to expand access to reproductive health care and birth control.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Says student debt must be deleted and plans to increase college savings accounts for vulnerable students.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: Student debt must be deleted. Party politics has scorched us, setting divisions in our democracy.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Plans to double childcare slots and create universal pre-K including before- and after-school care.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I will double the existing childcare slots, universal pre-K including the before- and after-school for all California kids.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Plans to set high standards for clean air and water, control carbon emissions, and expand renewable energy.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: As your Governor I will set the highest standards of clean air, water, environmental protection, controlling carbon emissions and expanding advanced renewable energy.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Says fracking and other exploration must follow the highest scientific standards rather than being banned outright.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: Fracking and other explorations must be in accordance with the highest scientific standards.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Supports strict background checks and stronger gun violence laws while stating support for the Second Amendment.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I am the greatest supporter of constitutional rights including 2nd amendment. However, I will not let that overtake public safety. I will enforce strict measures and background checks to prevent deadly weapons in wrong hands.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Opposes the death penalty.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I do not support death penalty.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Plans to seek federal funding and offer housing plans to ease down payment, mortgage, rent and utility costs.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I will seek federal funding to ease burdensome complexities and offer real housing plans to ease down payment, mortgage, rent and utilities.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Supports Rescue Ranch as a practical solution to homelessness.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I support Rescue Ranch as a practical solution to address homelessness and meet the essential needs of individuals seeking help.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Plans to stop price gouging and investigate price hikes on housing, rent, gas, and groceries.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: Upon getting elected, I will stop price gouging, investigate the price hike of all items including buying a home, renting, gas, grocery, home goods etc.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Plans to lower taxes and provide tax relief for businesses and job creators.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I'll lower taxes to lower costs and lead California in civil rights, best healthcare, income, education, trade, infrastructure and space age advancement.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Plans to ease regulations and offer relief to small businesses.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I will offer relief to small businesses from burdensome regulations and boost small business conditions for expansion.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Says California's water rights need resetting for its growing population and calls for water reforms.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: The water rights need resetting for our growing population. Water reforms are needed due to the water shortages to set a fair relief for all.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Supports universal mail-in ballots for all registered voters and an independent redistricting process.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: Universal mail-in ballots for all registered voters. A true independent, public riven redistricting process.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Plans to expand crime prevention resources and modern training for law enforcement to use force only as a last resort.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I will introduce modern-day training of law enforcement personnel to exercise extreme caution and use force as a last resort with necessary approval.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Plans to end harsh late fees, penalties, and high interest rates.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I will introduce every relief to cater the losses faced by the public with an end to hardship, unconstitutional harsh late fees, penalties, and harsh interest rates.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Plans to enforce and expand protections for animals from cruelty.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: We must continue with our fullest responsibility to care for and protect animals and increase the need for larger platforms to protect animals from cruelty.

ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.stance: Says the candidate strongly supports seniors through access to maximum healthcare and welfare benefits.
ca_gov_primary_raji_rab.quote: I strongly support our seniors by ensuring access to maximum healthcare and welfare benefits.

ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.stance: Reallocate education funding away from bureaucratic overhead and into classroom teacher pay.
ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.quote: California has failed vulnerable students at the most basic task: learning to read. We must aggressively reallocate funding away from bureaucratic overhead and directly into the pockets of the teachers working with students.

ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.stance: Mandate evidence-based reading and mathematics instruction statewide and strip away ideological teaching fads.
ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.quote: At the same time, we need to strip away ideological fads from our teaching methods and mandate evidence-based reading and mathematics instruction statewide (see my School Partisan Analysis for detailed numbers on district performance with regard to where things work better in California).

ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.stance: Would use declining K-12 enrollment to pay remaining teachers more while reducing other costs.
ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.quote: For example, with declining K-12 enrollment, we should take the opportunity to move funds elsewhere, or at the very least pay our remaining K-12 teachers more while reducing other costs.

ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.stance: Reduce regulatory barriers to building power grids, water reservoirs, and housing so utilities and housing are more affordable.
ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.quote: We must make it vastly easier and cheaper to build robust power grids, upgrade water reservoirs, and expand housing capacity so that basic utilities and housing are affordable for regular Californians.

ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.stance: Supports continuing recent CEQA reforms that address abuses blocking housing, with monitoring.
ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.quote: There has been recent progress (e.g., CEQA abuses that prevent housing from being built), but it needs to continue and be monitored.

ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.stance: Wants to redirect non-academic university resources back to the core teaching mission and reduce administrative bloat.
ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.quote: At Berkeley, I have petitioned leaders, presented analysis, and joined committees for a decade trying to optimize and redirect these resources back to our core mission.

ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.stance: Opposes mandating free tuition for the largely wealthy student population at Berkeley.
ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.quote: Simply mandating “free tuition” for the largely wealthy student population at Berkeley would amount to a massive financial handout to people who don’t need it.

ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.stance: Any government program should be measured against whether it beats simply giving people cash.
ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.quote: This may sound glib, but any potential solution should be measured against whether it would be better than just giving people cash.

ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.stance: Supports using the state, through Medi-Cal, to negotiate better prices against the health industry.
ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.quote: Individuals have no chance against the powerful health industry, whereas the state, through Medi-Cal, can negotiate a better deal.

ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.stance: Favors New York-style drug law overhaul and focused diversion-to-treatment programs to lower incarceration without sacrificing safety.
ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.quote: New York has proven that a state can drastically lower incarceration rates without sacrificing public safety, provided the government commits to focused, verifiable diversion programs rather than endlessly funding a massive prison bureaucracy.

ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.stance: Calls for careful auditing of high administrative costs in the prison system.
ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.quote: This suggests structurally high administrative costs that warrant careful auditing, particularly when evaluating resource allocation against other core state missions like public education.

ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.stance: Argues that supportive housing at People's Park-level costs is too expensive and that cheaper housing options would be better elsewhere.
ca_gov_primary_satish_rao.quote: The same housing would be substantially cheaper and perhaps more beneficial for many in other areas.

ca_gov_primary_scott_p_shields.stance: Shields states that social solutions are best achieved with capitalism and freedoms.
ca_gov_primary_scott_p_shields.quote: Social solutions are best achieved with capitalism and freedoms.

ca_gov_primary_scott_p_shields.stance: Shields states that social solutions should not come through socialism, communism, religious theocracies, or dictatorships.
ca_gov_primary_scott_p_shields.quote: Social solutions are always needed but not by way of socialism or communism or religious theocracies or dictatorships, which should all be classified as kingdom-hoods.

ca_gov_primary_scott_p_shields.stance: Shields states that separation of church and state is the only guard against a religious theocracy ruling in government.
ca_gov_primary_scott_p_shields.quote: Separation Of Church And State Was And Still Is The Only Guard Against A Religious Theocracy From Becoming The Rulers In Government.

ca_gov_primary_scott_p_shields.stance: Shields states that payola is the greatest economic sin because it creates collusion of powers that limits distribution.
ca_gov_primary_scott_p_shields.quote: Payola Is The Sin Of All Sins In Economic Society, As It Creates Collusion Of Powers To Limit Distribution.

ca_gov_primary_scott_p_shields.stance: Shields states that California should launch a California crypto coin to fill the void left by Warren Buffett's retirement.
ca_gov_primary_scott_p_shields.quote: With Your Retiring, It Will Be Hard To Fill That Void So We Have To Launch The California Crypto Coin And We Appreciate All You Have Done.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.stance: Steyer says California must build every type of home, from shelters and transitional housing to apartments, starter homes, and single-family homes.
ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: We must build every type of home to meet the needs of every Californian: from shelters and transitional housing, to encouraging and supporting the building of apartments and starter homes, as well as single family homes.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.stance: Steyer says he will close corporate tax loopholes and raise $20 billion in new revenue each year for education, healthcare, childcare, and home care.
ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: Tom is going to close these corporate loopholes, and raise $20 billion of new revenue each year to fund things like education, healthcare, childcare, and home care, all without charging working people a penny.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.stance: Steyer says universal healthy school meals will be funded year-round.
ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: We will ensure universal healthy school meals are funded year-round.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.stance: Steyer plans to work with the California Energy Commission to create an "affordability first framework" to avoid future supply shortages and price spikes.
ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: Over the long-term, I’ll work with the California Energy Commission and other policy leaders to create an “affordability first framework” to avoid future supply shortages and price spikes.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.stance: Steyer says he will ban utility contributions to candidates and reform state oversight of utilities.
ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: This includes banning utility contributions to candidates and reforming state oversight of utility companies to better serve the people of California.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.stance: Steyer says he will require data centers to ensure energy prices for families go down rather than up.
ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.quote: Tom will mandate that data centers ensure energy prices for families go down – not up.

ca_gov_primary_tom_steyer.stance: Steyer says he will ban social media for kids under 16.
